text:
30-day free trial
DX-CADTM: AI-powered 3D CAD for sheet metal, fabrication, industrial design and 3D printing
Draw it. Script it in Python. Or ask AI to build it.
One window for 2D drafting, 3D parts, assemblies, sheet metal and production drawings, for engineers, fabricators and makers. Use the AI your company approves, or none at all: IT decides. Unfold sheet metal for the laser and press brake, check parts before you 3D print them, and exchange STEP, DXF, STL and 3MF with any other CAD.
Download for Windows macOS, Linux and Python
Version 0.1.6, 13 November 2026. Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit), signed by Designmatix; builds for macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon Macs (M1 or later) and for Linux too. System requirements. Fabrication and Drafting Pro add-ons free during your trial.
A cut-away two-spool turbofan engine, modelled in DX-CAD in Python
What DX-CAD does
From a first sketch to the laser, the press brake or the 3D printer, with the files your customers and colleagues already use.
Sheet metal
Base flanges, flanges with returns and hems, corner treatments and relief. Flat patterns by K-factor, checked against hand calculations in DX-CAD's own test suite, and exported as DXF with one line per bend, ready for your CAM.Gauge tables per material, and shop export profiles for your own layer names.
3D printing
Check a part before you print it: overhangs, the thinnest wall and its mass in your chosen material. Export STL and 3MF, colours included.
Assemblies
Parts placed by mates (coincident, concentric, distance, angle), with mate suggestions you confirm; parts used from their own files; sub-assemblies. Identical parts are counted together in the bill of materials.
Drawings
Drawing documents that follow their model, on ISO and ANSI sheets from A4 to A0 with your title block. Views at their own scale, parts lists with part numbers and revisions, grouped hole callouts, and export to PDF and DXF.
Works beside SOLIDWORKS
STEP import and export that keeps assembly structure, names, colours and custom properties, and a SOLIDWORKS-style controls option for mouse and keys, so mixed teams can share work.SOLIDWORKS is a trademark of Dassault Systèmes. DX-CAD is not affiliated with or endorsed by Dassault Systèmes.
Models you can read
Every model is also a short Python script. Change a number and rebuild, keep variants under version control, and automate repetitive parts. The SDK for add-ons is open source.
Your choice of AI
Ask the built-in assistant to build or change a model and watch each step appear; one Undo takes it back. Use your own key with Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini or Azure OpenAI, or your own model on your own servers through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Agents such as Claude Desktop can drive DX-CAD through MCP.Claude is a trademark of Anthropic, PBC. OpenAI, Gemini and Azure are trademarks of their owners.
IT in control of AI
One policy setting, by Group Policy or a policy file, switches every AI feature off for the whole company, and DX-CAD then makes no connection to any AI service. Or allow only the providers and endpoints you have approved, such as your own Azure tenant, and decide whether model scripts, screenshots or photos may be sent. Users cannot override it, and the installer takes /NOAI for a rollout with no AI at all.
Fabrication add-on
Cones and reducers, square-to-rounds, hoppers, Y-pieces, lobster elbows and branches, dished heads, press-brake parts such as trays, boxes, brackets and corner posts, and weldments with cut lists. Each with its flat pattern and a marking table for setting out by hand.
Drafting Pro add-on
Dimensions, balloons, hole tables, tolerances and GD&T, surface texture and weld symbols, revision tables and notes, automatic dimensioning and ballooning, and section, detail, auxiliary, shaded and exploded views.

Does DX-CAD send my models to an AI service?
Only if you use the assistant with a provider your company allows, and only what the policy lets it send. With AI switched off by policy, DX-CAD makes no connection to any AI service.

title: A bracket with four holes, from a sentence | DX-CAD documentation | DX-CAD by Designmatix

headings.t: A bracket with four holes, from a sentence
The same part as a model

text:
DX-CAD documentation
A bracket with four holes, from a sentence
This is what an agent does with dxcad serve when it is given one sentence:
Make me a mounting bracket 80 long: a base 30 deep and an upright 46 high along its back edge, both 6 thick, with four 5 mm holes in a row through the base. Then make it 100 long, and save it.
Three files tell it. This page is the story; bracket.jsonl is the conversation itself, every request a client sends, one a line, from initialize to project_save; and bracket.py is the same part as a model. The test suite plays both, so what is written here is what the server does. How to point Claude Code or Claude Desktop at the server is in ../agents.md.
On this page
The section, extruded
Four holes in one call
Counting them
The same part as a model
Longer, without writing it again
Saved
Trying it
The section, extruded
The bracket is an L in section, so the agent draws the L on the YZ plane, base along Y and upright along Z, and extrudes it 80 along X:
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "sketch_extrude", "arguments": {"name": "bracket", "plane": "YZ", "profile": [{"op": "move_to", "point": [0, 0]}, {"op": "line_to", "point": [30, 0]}, {"op": "line_to", "point": [30, 46]}, {"op": "line_to", "point": [24, 46]}, {"op": "line_to", "point": [24, 6]}, {"op": "line_to", "point": [0, 6]}, {"op": "close"}], "height": 80}}}
The answer is the part's facts, which is the only look at it the agent gets: one valid solid of volume 33600.000, which is the L's area, 30 x 6 + 6 x 40 = 420, times 80; size 80 x 30 x 46; eight flat faces; no holes yet.
Four holes in one call
The agent does not work out four centres. It makes one drill, a cylinder of radius 2.5 through the base at the first hole, 10 from the end and half way across the 24 of base that the upright leaves clear:
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 4, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "make_cylinder", "arguments": {"name": "drill", "radius": 2.5, "height": 6, "origin": [10, 12, 0]}}}
and patterns it, four in a row 20 apart, cut from the bracket:
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "linear_pattern", "arguments": {"name": "drill", "step": [20, 0, 0], "count": 4, "cut_from": "bracket"}}}
The drill is taken out of the document afterwards, as a cutting tool should be, and the whole call is one undo. The answer is the bracket again: volume 33128.761, which is 33600 less four cylinders of pi x 2.5 x 2.5 x 6, and twelve faces, eight flat and four cylindrical.
Counting them
An agent that was asked for four holes has to be able to count them:
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 6, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "describe", "arguments": {"name": "bracket"}}}
describe answers, among the rest, "holes": four of them, each of diameter 5 and depth 6, along Z, through, with centres at x = 10, 30, 50 and 70, y =
That is the sentence, checked.
The same part as a model
Every DX-CAD™ model is a script. The agent writes the part down as one, bracket.py, whose numbers are names at the top of the file, and runs it with run_model. That tool and model_set run Python, so the server must have been started with --allow-run; without it both are refused. The server answers "changed": []: the model builds, to the last face, the bracket the tools had already made. The document now carries the model, so the project saved from it is parametric.
Longer, without writing it again
model_values lists the numbers the model is made of, LENGTH, DEPTH, HEIGHT, THICKNESS, HOLES, HOLE_DIAMETER and INSET. To make the bracket 100 long the agent changes one of them and the server runs the model again:
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 9, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "model_set", "arguments": {"values": {"LENGTH": 100}}}}
The model spaces its holes from the length, so they move with it: the bracket is now 100 x 30 x 46 with a volume of 41528.761, which is 420 x 100 less the same four cylinders, and a last describe still counts four holes of diameter 5, now at x = 10, 36.667, 63.333 and 90. One undo would put back the 80 bracket and the old text together.
Saved
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 11, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "project_save", "arguments": {"path": "bracket.dxcprt"}}}
bracket.dxcprt lands in the server's working directory. It opens in the window with dxcad gui bracket.dxcprt, model and all, and dxcad describe bracket.dxcprt says in words what the agent was told in JSON.
Trying it
With nothing but a shell, from this directory:
dxcad serve --allow-run < bracket.jsonl
Without --allow-run the run_model and model_set requests are refused.
prints one reply a line and leaves bracket.dxcprt behind.

text:
DX-CAD documentation
Where the fastener figures come from
Most of the numbers in these models are shape: how long a plate is, how thick a wall is, how far apart two holes sit. Those are chosen, and changing one is the whole point of a parametric model.
A few are not chosen. A hole that an M4 screw has to pass through, a drill that an M4 thread is cut into, a seat that an M4 socket head has to sit in: each of those has one right answer and it comes out of a table. This page is that table for every such figure in the examples, so that nobody has to guess whether a number was looked up or made up.
Every row was checked against its standard by hand on 2026-09-21.

The three holes one thread asks for
One thread size asks for three different holes, and the table's rows are each one of them.
The clearance hole. The screw passes through and does not bite, so the hole is larger than the thread. ISO 273 gives three series: fine 8.4, medium 9.0 and coarse 10.0 for M8. flange.py takes the medium one, which is what a part with ordinary tolerances wants.
The tapping drill. The thread is cut into this hole, so it is smaller than the thread: the nominal diameter less the pitch, which for M4 coarse is 4.0 - 0.7, a 3.3 drill (ISO 2306).
The counterbore. A socket head screw's seat has to clear its head across and in height, to sink the head below the face: for an M4 ISO 4762 screw, whose head is 7.0 across and 4.0 high, DIN 974-1 gives 8.0 across, and 4.4 deep leaves 0.4 over it.

These name a thread and take its nominal diameter, which is not what any of the tables above would give. They are here so that nobody reads them as looked-up numbers.

Example parts
Every part here is a model.py: a short Python script with its numbers at the top. Every name the kernel and the sketch API have is already in scope, so a model imports nothing. To build one into a project, and to look at it:
dxcad run bracket.py --output bracket.dxcprt
dxcad describe bracket.dxcprt
dxcad gui bracket.py
Change a number and run it again: that is the whole of DX-CAD™'s parametric model. The test suite runs every model on this page, checks each part it builds against arithmetic, and builds it again with one number changed, so what is written here is what the script does.
A sketch is drawn on a plane. Plane.XY, Plane.XZ and Plane.YZ are the three standard ones, Plane.XY.offset(z) is XY lifted by z, which is what engine_inline4.py draws its bolt heads on, and Plane.from_face(face) is the plane of a face of a part already built.

Seven of them show what v0.1 adds: sheet metal with relief and holes (relieved_tray.py) and dimensioned to the outside (channel.py), parts placed by mates (mated_enclosure.py, bolt_mate.py), a sub-assembly used twice (door.py), raised text (the nameplate of gearbox.py) and a drawing document (drawn_bracket.py). Two keep a file beside them: door.py uses door-hinge.dxcasm, and drawn_bracket.dxcdrg is the bracket's drawing. dxcad examples door copies the file along with the model.
Five are whole machines of some two hundred to four hundred parts each: gearbox.py, engine_inline4.py, robot_arm.py, race_car_frame.py and steel_structure.py. Each opens drawn light, so that it builds in a few seconds, and its docstring names the numbers that draw it in full: the gear teeth's involutes, the cam lobes, the bores of the suspension tubes, the bolts on every end plate.
Some of the numbers in these models are not chosen but looked up: a clearance hole, a tapping drill, the seat a screw head sits in. dimensions.md says where each of those comes from.
The bracket is also the worked example for agents: bracket.md tells the story of an agent making it through dxcad serve, and bracket.jsonl is that conversation, line for line.
From the DX-CAD documentation, examples/README.md. All the pages.

title: The window | DX-CAD documentation | DX-CAD by Designmatix
text:
DX-CAD documentation
The window
dxcad gui opens the viewer: an OpenCASCADE scene on the left, the model.py in a pane on the right, and the output of the last run under it. Everything the window does to a document is an edit that can be undone, and everything it builds it builds through the same kernel the command line uses.
The window is the one part of DX-CAD™ that needs a display. Every other command runs on a machine with none.
On this page
Opening it
Tabs
The menus
The help window
The panels
The dialogs
Keyboard shortcuts
The model pane
The model a project carries
Opening it
On nothing, on a project, or on a model.py. These three are the whole of it:
dxcad examples bracket
dxcad run bracket.py --output bracket.dxcprt
dxcad gui
dxcad gui bracket.dxcprt
dxcad gui bracket.py
dxcad-gui opens the same window with no console behind it, which is what a desktop shortcut points at. Every command here is in cli.md.
A file that cannot be opened is never met with silence (item 803). Started on one, by any of these names or by a double click in Explorer, DX-CAD brings its window up with nothing open and a box that names the file, why it cannot be opened (it does not exist; it is not a DX-CAD project; for a STEP file that does not read, the STEP reader's own error) and what would work. The same words go to the log and the output pane, and the exit status is 2 once the window is shut. A STEP file is not opened as a project: dxcad import makes a project of it, and a model's import_step reads it. With a window already open, that window says it instead, once. If DX-CAD cannot start at all, a message box of the system's own says why in one line and where the log is.
When anything keeps the window busy for a second, a large drawing being drawn, a model being built, an add-on's command, a small "Please wait" window appears over it with what is being done, and stays a second after the work ends so it never blinks away; a command that takes under a second never shows it. While a model builds it has a Cancel button, which ends the run with the document as it was, as Stop on the status bar and Esc do.
A message too long for the status bar is cut with "...", and its whole text is kept: it is the bar's tooltip, and a click on the bar opens it in full in a small box with Copy and Close, so the end of a long refusal, what to do about it, is never lost. A message that fits has neither.
Work that knows its steps says how far it has got: drawing a sheet's views (view n of N) and exporting a drawing, each of its sheets' views a step. It shows a bar with the percent done and, once at least 5 percent is done and 5 seconds have passed, the time left ("About 3 minutes left": whole minutes above a minute, tens of seconds below). Work whose steps are not known, such as a model build, shows a moving bar and the time so far ("2 min 10 s so far"), never a made-up percent. An export can be cancelled too: Cancel stops it at its next view, no file is written, nothing is changed, and the status bar says "Cancelled: nothing was changed". Work that cannot stop shows no Cancel. The window stays the size it is whatever it says.
Tabs
Several documents can be open at once, one tab each (item 570). Each tab has its own parts, model pane, undo history and file name, and the Parts and History docks, the title bar and the actions follow the tab in front. The tabs show above the view once there are two; drag one to move it, and Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab step through them. The button at the tabs' right, or Window > Tile, shows them side by side instead. Closing the window asks once for each tab with unsaved changes. With a window open, dxcad gui FILE or a double click on a part, assembly or drawing file hands the file to that window as a tab. An agent over dxcad serve --window works on the tab in front, and each result names it.
The menus
One section per menu, in the order the menu bar has them, and one row per action. A shortcut is written as Qt writes it, so Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux is Cmd+Shift+S on a Mac; an action with no shortcut has an empty cell. The test suite reads the menu bar offscreen and holds this list to it, row for row.
The menus and toolbars follow the tab in front (item 856). A command that does not apply to it is greyed, not hidden, so the menus keep their shape, and the pointer over it says why: a Model or Sheet Metal command on a drawing's tab says "Open a part or assembly for Flange", a Drawing command on a part's says "Needs a drawing tab: open a drawing for Add View", and a Sketch tool with no sketch in progress "Start a sketch for Line". Files, Undo, Redo, Delete, Zoom Window, Measure, the panels, the window and Help apply on every tab. A command that applies but is greyed for want of something says what it needs, such as "Fuse: Needs two parts or more". An add-on's command is greyed the same way where it says it does not apply.
File
Action
Shortcut
What it does
New Part
Ctrl+N
An empty part in a new tab, with the model pane holding the template a new model starts from. A tab with nothing open is started again instead. It is saved as a part file, .dxcprt.
New Assembly
An empty assembly in a new tab, saved as an assembly file, .dxcasm: the model pane shows how parts are used from their own files with use() and placed with place(), and the Parts dock opens.
New Drawing
A drawing of the saved part or assembly in front, on the default sheet, in a tab of its own, saved as a drawing file, .dxcdrg; as Drawing... does at its default size.
Open...
Ctrl+O
Open a part, assembly or drawing file (.dxcprt, .dxcasm or .dxcdrg; an older .dxcad or .dxcaddrg opens as one of them) in a tab of its own; a file already open brings its tab forward. Nothing in it is run: a carried model is asked about at the first Run, unless it was trusted before with Trust This Project's Model.
Open Recent
The last 10 files opened or saved, newest first, each by its name with its full path as a tooltip and numbered 1 to 9 and 0 for the keyboard; kept from one session to the next. Opening or saving a file moves it to the top. A file that is gone is shown in italics, marked (not found); choosing it says so and takes it off the list. Clear Recent empties it, leaving a greyed No recent files. A file opens in a tab, as Open's does.
Close
Close the current tab, as its cross does; the last tab is put back as New leaves it: no parts, no model, no name, and any sketch ended. Unsaved changes are asked about first. Greyed while nothing is open.
Save
Ctrl+S
Write the document, and the pane's model with it, back where it came from; in a drawing's tab, the drawing as a .dxcdrg. A file opened as an older .dxcad or .dxcaddrg is saved in its new type beside it, the old file kept.
Save As...
Ctrl+Shift+S
Write the document to another file, which becomes the window's own.
Save Model
Ctrl+Shift+M
Write the pane's text back to the model.py it was opened from, and nothing else.
Version History...
The model's versions, newest first: each save, each run after an edit and each change the Assistant makes keeps one in the project, with its time, who made it (you, or the Assistant with the first line of what it was asked) and one line saying what changed; the last 200, the oldest let go first. A chosen version is compared with the pane as text, the lines taken out and put in. Restore builds it, one undo step, and keeps it as a new version; Save as .py... writes it to a file. No key or token is kept in a version.
Export Model...
Write the pane's text to a new .py file, which the window then follows.
Import Model...
Read a model.py into the pane, leaving the document as it is until the next Run.
Import...
Bring a STEP file or a DXF drawing in through the Import wizard: the file, its format read from what it holds; a check of what it holds before anything is added; how it is placed; a summary, and Finish writes it into the model, one step for Undo. After a DXF the window works in 2D drafting, and after a STEP in 3D modelling; File > Settings... > Mode switches back. A DWG is refused: save it as DXF from the program that made it.
Export Drawing...
In a drawing's tab, write its sheet as a PDF or a DXF, as dxcad drawing does. Otherwise write the sketch being drawn, or else every Sketch the model names, as a DXF or an SVG drawing by the extension given, in millimetres, one layer or group per sketch: lines, arcs, circles, ellipses and splines each written as themselves.
Export Parts...
Write the picked parts, or every part when none is picked, to one STEP, STL, 3MF, BREP or glTF binary (.glb) file, by the filter chosen or the name's ending, as dxcad export writes them; a 3MF keeps each part a named object, and a .glb each part a named node in its colour and place, meshed as the 3D view meshes it, for web pages and other 3D tools. Greyed with no part, hidden in 2D drafting.
Drawing...
Make a drawing of the saved project in a tab of its own, on a sheet asked for, A4 to A1 or one of the ten ISO and ANSI sheets, as dxcad drawing draws one: the front, top, right and isometric views with hidden edges dashed, at one scale that fits, in the title block with the project, file, date, scale and sheet size filled in, and the bill of materials as a parts list. Each hole a view sees round may have its centre lines: Centre marks in Drawing properties, off on a new drawing unless the model calls centre_marks(True). The drawing is a document of its own: drag a view to move it, the view and its sizes and label following the pointer while it moves, one undo entry when it is let go and Esc putting it back mid-drag; the top and right views stay in line with the front, moving with it, the top only up and down and the right only sideways, unless Unlock Alignment (on the view's right-click menu, or In line with the front view in Drawing properties) lets one move freely, Lock Alignment putting it back in line; right-click a view to show or hide its dashed hidden lines, and right-click the sheet for its scale, its title block fields and whether the dimensions and the parts list are shown, each one undo entry. While a drawing's tab is in front, the left dock shows Drawing properties: the sheet's size, its Title Block... and the parts list's columns, ticked and dragged into order (Item, Part number, Description, Material, Qty and Rev by default, Size and Mass to be had; the description and material are a part's own description and material properties when it has them), remembered for new drawings and for the bill's Save CSV..., and for the view clicked on the sheet its label and hidden lines. The scale is two number fields, 1 : N or N : 1 with any positive numbers (1 : 25, 1 : 7.5, 2 : 1), the standard ratios offered beside them and To fit as a button; it is applied as it is typed, after a short pause and without Enter, the title block following, and a field that is not a number above 0 is marked red and changes nothing. With a view clicked, the scale typed is that view's own: it alone is drawn at it, with its centre lines and hole callouts, its label says it ("TOP SCALE 1 : 10"), and the title block keeps the sheet's; To fit gives it the sheet's scale again. Save writes it as a .dxcdrg, which holds the project's path and no geometry, so the sheet is drawn again from the project whenever the drawing is opened or its tab comes forward, and the status bar says so; a project that is gone is named by its path. Export Drawing writes it as a PDF or DXF. A project not yet saved is asked to be saved first. Greyed with no part, hidden in 2D drafting.
Export 3D Web Page...
The parts as one .html file that anyone can open in a browser or on a phone, with no CAD, no plugin and no internet: they turn, pan and zoom the model, pick a named view (the view on screen when you exported it first, then Front, Top, Right and Isometric), show or hide each part in its list, and measure between two corners in mm (3D web pages). The page is made at each fineness first under a bar with Cancel, so the question that follows, Normal (as the 3D view), Coarse or Fine, gives the size of the file each makes; then name the file. It is written beside its name and renamed when complete; Cancel at any step leaves no file. Nothing in the model changes. dxcad export-web writes the same page from the command line. Greyed with no part, hidden in 2D drafting.
Export 3D PDF...
The parts as a PDF with one landscape page, A4, A3 or Letter, whose model turns, pans, zooms and measures in Adobe Acrobat Reader once the reader clicks Trust this document, each part named in its model tree, with named views: the view on screen when you exported it, the default, then Front, Top, Right and Isometric (3D PDF). Readers with no 3D, browsers among them, show a picture of the default view instead; a line under the model names the project, DX-CAD's version and the date, and says lengths are in mm. Pick the paper, name the file, and the PDF is made under a bar with Cancel; it is written beside its name and renamed when complete, and Cancel at any step leaves no file. Nothing in the model changes. dxcad export-3dpdf writes the same kind of file from the command line. Greyed with no part, hidden in 2D drafting.
Send to Slicer
Write the picked entry, or every entry when none is picked, to a 3MF and open it in the slicer, which is asked for once and remembered.
Where Used...
On a saved file: the assemblies and drawings in a folder chosen, and every folder below it, that use this file, each with how many copies it holds, as dxcad where-used lists them. Every part keeps a stable id through renames, so an assembly that uses a part by its old name still finds it, saying the new name in the model's output.
Title Block...
The fields a person fills in once for every drawing: company, drawn by, checked by, material, finish, general tolerance, drawing number and revision, and since item 974 every other text a title block shows, the title, scale, date and the others the sheet fills itself among them, each left blank to stay automatic; and the font the drawing is lettered in, the bundled DejaVuSans (the default) or any TrueType font the system has, with the height of its dimensions, labels and fields, 2.5, 3.5, 5 or 7 mm. Kept from one session to the next and used by every sheet File > Drawing makes.
Trust This Project's Model
Trust the model the project in front carried, so it runs here with no question. Kept in the settings by the project's path and the SHA-256 of the model's text, never the text: opening the same file with the same model is trusted again, and any other model at that path is asked about. Answering Trust and run at the question does the same; a trusted project saved keeps its trust for the text saved. The model pane's header says whether a carried model is trusted. Greyed unless the model in front came in a file and is not trusted.
Revoke Trust in This Project's Model
Forget that trust: the model is asked about again before it runs. Greyed unless the model in front is trusted.
Settings...
Settings, in groups. Mode, the first, is 2D drafting or 3D modelling, 3D modelling at the start: 2D drafting hides every action that acts on a solid (Extrude, Revolve, Edit > Mirror's part option, Sketch on Face, the printability actions and Send to Slicer) and names itself in the title, and 3D modelling shows everything. The mode changes the window only, not the kernel, the command line or the agent door, and is remembered between runs. View, the second, holds Show Planes and After a run (item 964): Keep the Camera, Fit the Model (the default) or Follow New Parts, the parts new or changed since the last run (all of them the first time), with Fill, from 0.5 to 1.2 and 1.0 at first, the share of the view's tighter side the parts fill; every fit after a run follows it, F5, Run on Change, the window's build commands, the end of an Assistant turn and the fit after an agent's quiet spell, while a model opened on its own keeps its first framing, and Keep the Camera leaves the view as it is and does not turn it; Runs (item 977), the seconds a run of the model is given before it is stopped, 60 at first and from 5 to 3600, which an agent's run in the window and a drawing export's run are held to as well, Model > No Time Limit setting it aside, and Let Claude run models from Claude Desktop (item 988), the answer to the question Connect Claude Desktop asks once, which writes this copy's link again to match; Recovery, the minutes between keeps of the unsaved tabs; Parts, the Default material: what a part with no material of its own is made of, mild steel as shipped, which the Parts dock and the Bill of Materials mark "(default)" (a sheet part is its spec's metal); Updates, Check for updates at start, on as shipped (Help > Check for Updates). On macOS it is under the application menu. Controls (item 686) is DX-CAD's own or Classic CAD controls (middle-button orbit): under the second the middle button rotates, Ctrl+middle pans and Shift+middle and the wheel zoom, the left button only picks, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+7 are Front, Back, Left, Right, Top, Bottom and Iso, Ctrl+8 Normal To, and in the 3D view F fits, Space shows the View Selector and S the Shortcut Bar. The first start asks "Used to another CAD program?" once. Under the presets, Zoom about the cursor is View > Zoom About the Cursor (item 963). Under either preset the arrow keys pan the 3D view while it has the focus, a tenth of the view a press and a hundredth with Shift, and not while the script pane or another field has it.
Quit
Close the window, asking first when there is an unsaved edit.
Edit
Action
Shortcut
What it does
Undo
Ctrl+Z
Take back the last edit to the document, the model pane following it.
Redo
Ctrl+Y
Put back the last edit that was undone.
Rename...
Give the picked entry another name, which the model is rewritten to match. A part made in a loop or a helper is renamed by a rename() statement after the parts.
Duplicate
A copy of the picked entry, under a name of its own, set its own width along x and left picked.
Move...
Move the picked part by dragging it in the view: after Move, press and drag, and the part follows the pointer in the plane of the screen, drawn where it would go with how far beside the pointer; let go and it is put there, one undo step, its line in the model wrapped in translate. Hold X, Y or Z to keep the drag to that axis of the model. Type a number for the distance instead, along the axis held or the way the drag is going, and Enter puts the part there. Esc leaves it where it was. A part held by mates moves only along what they leave it free to do, on its face or along its axis; where they leave nothing it does not move, and the status bar names the mate that holds it.
Mirror...
Add the picked entry mirrored in the XY, XZ or YZ plane, or in the picked face when one planar face is picked, as a part of its own after the original, writing mirror into the model.
Delete
Del
Take the picked entries out of the document.
Select Category...
Pick every element whose type is in one category, chosen from the categories the model's elements are in (element_type and values_of, item 1145). Greyed when no element has a type.
Go to Line...
Ctrl+G
Put the caret in the model pane on a line, given as 120, or on a line and column, 120:5, each counted from 1, the line centred. A line past the end goes to the last line; anything else says what it takes.
Find...
Ctrl+F
Open the Find bar under the model pane, holding the words selected in it: every match highlighted and "n of m" said, with Match Case, Whole Word and Regular Expression. Enter or F3 finds the next match, Shift+Enter or Shift+F3 the previous, wrapping round the end and saying so; an expression that is not one is named in the bar. Escape closes it and takes the highlights away.
Find Next
F3
The next match of the Find bar's words after the caret, wrapping round.
Find Previous
Shift+F3
The match before the caret, wrapping round.
Replace...
Ctrl+H
The Find bar with a Replace field: Replace (or Enter in the field) changes the match the caret is on and finds the next; Replace All changes every match as one step, one Undo taking it all back, and says how many. Match Case and Whole Word are honoured, and with Regular Expression \1 and \g<name> in the replacement are the match's groups.
View
Action
Shortcut
What it does
Fit
Frame everything the document holds.
Zoom About the Cursor
Off at first. While ticked the wheel zooms about the point under the cursor, the part there or the point on the plane the view turns about, which stays where it is on screen; unticked it zooms about the middle of the view. Also in Settings, under Controls. Kept for the next start.
Fit Selection
Shift+F
Frame the parts selected in the 3D view, keeping the view direction: they fill the view's tighter side to 1 / 1.15, centred. With nothing selected it frames every part shown. Also on the view's right-click menu.
Zoom Window
W
Drag a rectangle in the 3D view and it zooms to fit it, keeping the orientation: the rectangle is fitted at the depth of the nearest part under its centre (or of the parts' middle when nothing is there), its larger side filling the view; on a drawing's sheet the sheet does the same. Esc lets the rectangle go, and a click without a drag does nothing. Also on the View toolbar.
Measure
Measure by picking, in the 3D view, in a sketch being drawn (its own lines can be picked) and on a drawing's sheet, where a view's scale gives the model's sizes. It stays on until Esc. One pick: an edge's length; a circle's or an arc's radius and diameter; a face's area; a point's place. Two picks: the least distance between them with its dX, dY and dZ, the distance between their centres where both are circles or arcs, and the angle between two straight edges or flat faces. A third click starts again. A pick snaps to a vertex, the middle of an edge or the centre of a circle or an arc of what is under the pointer, with a marker there before the click. The status bar says what to pick ("Measure: pick a point, edge or face - Esc to finish") and then each measurement on a line ("Distance 60.000 mm dX 60.000 dY 0 dZ 0"). The measurement is said by the picks and in the Measure panel, which opens on the left as a tab over the parts' properties and shuts when Measure ends; its Copy puts it on the clipboard. Sizes are in millimetres, to three decimals or a drawing's own. The button stays pressed while Measure is on, and pressing it again ends it. Nothing is added to the model, and no tolerance is checked. Also on the View toolbar.
Fit Sheet
On a drawing tab, show the whole sheet again. The sheet also zooms at the cursor with the wheel and pans with a middle drag, and keeps its zoom when it is drawn again.
Front
Look along +Y.
Back
Look along -Y.
Left
Look along +X.
Right
Look along -X.
Top
Look down from +Z.
Bottom
Look up from -Z.
Iso
The three-quarter view a part is usually drawn in.
Normal To
Look square at the picked planar face, from the side it faces; with none picked the status bar says to pick one. Ctrl+8 under the classic CAD controls.
View Selector
A pop-up of the seven views and Normal To at the cursor; Space in the 3D view under the classic CAD controls.
Shortcut Bar
A pop-up at the cursor of the eight commands used most this session, most first, made up from Save, Undo, Redo, Fit, Iso, Run Script, Mate and Duplicate; S in the 3D view under the classic CAD controls.
Show Planes
Show or hide the three principal planes, XY, XZ and YZ: large, very faint squares about the origin, each tinted as the triad axis that stands out of it, the plane being sketched on a little stronger. Each fades as the view turns it edge on, over about a fifth of a second, and is not drawn at all edge on. Hidden, the plane a sketch is open on still shows. Also on the view's right-click menu and in File > Settings; remembered between runs, on at the first.
Explode...
Draw the parts moved apart for an exploded view: each away from the assembly's centre of mass by the factor asked times its distance from it, 0 being assembled. Only the drawing moves; picking, measuring and every edit act on the real parts, and a click on a part as it is drawn picks it. Hidden in 2D drafting.
Hide
H
Hide the picked parts: they are not drawn and a click goes through them. Their rows in the Parts dock stay, greyed, with their eye unticked; the eye ticks or unticks one part, and the dock's right-click menu has Hide or Show for the part under it, Hide Others and Show All. Also on the view's right-click menu. Hiding is a view's state: nothing is written into the model, no undo step is made, and the file keeps the parts hidden.
Show
Show the picked hidden parts again, a part picked from its greyed row in the Parts dock.
Hide Others
Hide every part but the picked ones. Also on the view's right-click menu.
Show All
Shift+H
Show every hidden part again. Also on the view's and the Parts dock's right-click menus.
Section View
Cut the view with a plane, XY, XZ or YZ through the parts' middle or a picked face's plane, also on the Display toolbar: the side beyond the plane is not drawn and the cut faces are capped, hatched in each part's colour. Picking and measuring work on the cut view. Only the view changes, never the model; Esc or Section View again ends it. While it is on, a banner across the top of the view says so, with Turn off, and the cutting plane is drawn faintly; hidden parts and an exploded view are said the same way. The section is the document's: it stays with its file, a new file and an example start without one, and a file saved with one opens with it and its banner (Settings and their scope).
Section Offset...
Move the cutting plane along its normal by the distance typed, from where it started.
Flip Section
Show the other side of the cut, the plane where it is.
Continuous Orbit
Ctrl+Shift+O
While ticked, also on the Display toolbar, a drag let go keeps the view turning the way and as fast as it was dragged, until a click, Esc or any view command. The model is not rebuilt.
Turntable...
Spin the view steadily about the vertical axis, slow, medium or fast, for a presentation or a recording; untick, click, Esc or a view command stops it. Settings > View > Stop spinning when DX-CAD loses focus, on at first, stops either when another window takes the focus.
Turn the Model After a Run
Ticked at first. When Run Script (F5), an Assistant turn or a run of calls from Claude Desktop has built parts and ended without error, the view is fitted to everything, at the angle it is at, and then turned at the turntable's slow speed to show the model off; a press, the wheel or any key in the view stops it and leaves the view where it is, and does nothing else. Unticked, the view is only fitted. A run on change, made while you are at something else, fits and never turns; a run that fails, or that changes no part, leaves the view alone.
Animate...
A short video of the model, for a presentation or a web page, from the view on screen: the Animate box (The Animate box) offers three choices, Explode and back (the parts come apart as an exploded view, hold, and come back together), Turn around (the camera goes once round the model) and Build it up (the parts arrive one at a time in the model's order); a tick, and turn while it moves, adds a turn to the first and the last; the Length, 3 to 30 seconds, 8 at first; the Size, Video 720p, Video 1080p, Square or Small GIF; and the Format, MP4 (H.264) or GIF. Preview plays it small in the box, looping, as it will be saved. Save... asks for the file and writes it under a bar with Cancel, which stops it and leaves no file. The parts move only as an exploded view or a camera moves them: no joints, no mates, never a feature before and after a change. Also on the Display toolbar; dxcad animate makes the same videos from the command line (dxcad animate). The recipes, sizes and formats, with a GIF of each recipe: Animations.
Shaded with Edges
Draw every part shaded with its face boundaries outlined. The mode at the start.
Shaded
Draw every part shaded, without its edges.
Wireframe
Draw every part as its edges alone.
Translucent
Draw every part shaded with edges at about half opacity, so what is inside can be seen.
Orthographic
Draw the 3D view without perspective, parallel edges parallel on screen, at the size perspective shows at the point the view turns about, so the switch does not jump there. Fit, the wheel, pan, orbit and Zoom Window work as in perspective. The document's saved view keeps it, and the last one chosen is how a new window starts.
Perspective
Draw the 3D view in perspective, as DX-CAD always has: what is nearer is larger. A file saved before Orthographic opens in perspective.
Theme
Light or Dark, switched at once and remembered between runs; light at the first. Light grades the background from white down to a pale grey-blue and draws a part with no colour of its own in steel blue-grey, outlined in near black; Dark grades from slate to near black and draws parts in pale blue-grey, outlined in near white. The sketch being drawn and its dimensions take a colour that reads on each. dxcad render --theme draws in either.
Script
Show or hide the model pane.
Output
Show or hide the output pane under it.
Parts
Show or hide the Parts dock on the left: the document's parts in model.py's order, a sub-assembly's parts listed under it as a tree, each with the operation that made it (extrude, revolve, fuse, place, hole...) and its placement when it was placed. Clicking a part picks it and puts the model pane's cursor on its statement, and a pick in the view marks its row. History

Assistant
Ctrl+Shift+A
Show or hide the Assistant dock, along the bottom of the 3D view until it is moved (after an update from a version that kept it down the side it is moved to the bottom once, and then stays where it is put), "Assistant (powered by Claude)", also on the Display toolbar: type a request and Claude builds or changes the document in front with DX-CAD's own tools, each step shown in the chat, written into the model and one Undo, a render shown inline. It uses your own Anthropic API key (Set Key, or Settings > Assistant's own API key field with Save Key, Forget Key and Test), kept encrypted for you by Windows, in the login Keychain on macOS and by the Secret Service (secret-tool) on Linux, and for the session where neither can; Test makes one small request and says whether it connected and how many models the provider lists, or that the key, the address or the network is wrong, and fills the Model list with the provider's own models, as Refresh beside it does (OpenAI's embedding, speech, transcription, image and moderation models left out), kept with the date for when nothing can be read; nothing is sent until you enable it, and the first use says what is sent (PRIVACY.md). While a turn runs, an hourglass drawn as a wireframe turns a quarter between steps (still when Windows' animations are off), a bar shows the steps done over the steps Claude planned, and a line says what is happening now, also on the status bar while the dock is shut. Stop ends a turn; the tokens each turn used show under the chat; Settings > Assistant chooses the provider (your own Anthropic key; OpenAI; Azure OpenAI, a deployment in your company's own tenant; Google Gemini; an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, such as a company gateway or a local model under Ollama or LM Studio, which needs no key; or the DX-CAD account), its model (for Azure OpenAI the deployment's name) and its address; the dock's title names the provider, keys are kept per provider, each provider's note on what it is sent shows the first time it is used, and switching keeps the chat. Each document has its own chat. Asked to change a part by its name ("add returns to sheet"), an answer that builds the part again under a new name where the part is asks first, with nothing written yet, whether to change the part or make a copy: Yes changes the part itself, its solid and its line in the model, and No keeps it and places the new part beside it, 20 mm clear, named as a copy; a request that asks for a copy in so many words gets the copy without the question. Either way the answer is one Undo.
Start Page

The Python with a console (python.exe) and the one without (pythonw.exe) of one folder are one copy, and the one written is always the first, whichever started the window. The page is up when DX-CAD starts with nothing open and when the last tab closes, and gives way the moment a document opens.
Toolbars
Show or hide each of the six toolbars: View (Fit, Zoom Window, Measure and the seven views), Display (the four modes, Section View, Continuous Orbit, the Assistant and Animate), Edit (Undo, Redo, Rename, Duplicate, Delete), Sketch (the drawing tools, then the sketch actions), Operations (Run Script, Extrude, Revolve, Fuse, Cut, Common, Pattern) and Sheet Metal (Base Flange, Flange, Export Flat Pattern, Show Flat Pattern). Then one toolbar for each menu, so that every menu command is also on a toolbar: File Menu, Edit Menu, View Menu, Model Menu, Sketch Menu, Sheet Metal Menu, Drawing Menu, Window Menu and Help Menu, each with every command of its menu that the six above do not have, in the menu's order, each with an icon of its own. They are hidden until you switch them on here, in View > Toolbars. The same list is on the right-click menu of any toolbar; the choice is remembered between runs. On every start the toolbars stand from the top left in the menus' order: File Menu, then Edit Menu and Edit, View Menu, View and Display, Model Menu and Operations, Sketch Menu and Sketch, Sheet Metal Menu and Sheet Metal, Drawing Menu, Window Menu and Help Menu, and last each add-on's, in the order of its menu; one switched off leaves no gap, and one dragged elsewhere is back in its place at the next start. When the window is too narrow for them in one row, the toolbars wrap to the next. A toolbar button has the toolbar's own grey background, and a checked one (the view looked from, the display mode, Measure while it is on) a pale blue one with a blue edge.
Toolbars...
Every toolbar in one box, the Toolbars box, in the order they stand: tick the ones to show, or Show All or Hide All, and OK shows and hides them together; Cancel changes nothing. Also from the Toolbars... button in File > Settings.
Reset Layout
Put every dock back where a fresh install has it: the model pane on the right, the output pane and the Assistant under it along the bottom, Parts, History and the drawing's properties as tabs on the left with the Feature Tree under them, none floating. Which docks are open stays as it is. The Assistant's remembered place and height are forgotten, so it opens along the bottom at the next start too.

Adopt Parts

Save to Its Own File
On an assembly, with one part picked that the assembly's own model builds (a virtual part): write it as a part file, NAME.dxcprt, beside the assembly, and replace its statement in the model with place(NAME, use("NAME.dxcprt", part=NAME)), so the assembly uses it from there, where it was; one Undo takes the statement back. Fuse
Make the picked parts (two or more; Ctrl+click adds one) one new part, fuse by name. The inputs stay in the model as plain variables the new part's line is built from. Also on the Operations toolbar; hidden in 2D drafting.
Cut
As Fuse, taking the other picked parts away from the first picked. On a sheet part a through cut normal to one face, round, rectangular or a rounded slot in any direction, and clear of the bends, is kept as that face's hole, cutout or slot, and the part stays sheet metal with no question. Such a prism through one face that runs on across a bend is cut as it will be bent, its outline on that face carried onto the flat and wrapped round the bend, as the shop floor cuts it on the flat and then folds it, since the straight tool's bite into a bend unfolds to no outline: the part stays sheet metal, nothing is asked, the status bar says "Cut across the bend as it will be bent: cut on the flat, then folded." and one Undo puts it back (item 923); see sheetmetal.md. A through cut of any other outline of lines and arcs normal to one face, clear of its edges and the bends, such as a window with rounded corners, is kept as that face's cut-out, its arcs cut as true arcs in the flat's DXF (item 959). Any other across a bend or a corner is refused, and any other cut asks whether to lose the flat.
Common
As Fuse, keeping only where the picked parts overlap; parts that do not meet are refused.
Pattern...
Repeat the one picked part as one new part, pattern by name: linear (along X, Y or Z, how many, how far apart), circular (about X, Y or Z through the origin, how many, over what angle) or grid (how many along X and along Y, how far apart each way). The original stays in the model as a plain variable the pattern's line is built from. A count below 2 is refused. Hidden in 2D drafting.
Pattern Feature...
Repeat the picked part's drilled feature, a hole, countersink or counterbore whose centre the model gives as world= numbers, across the same part, asked as Pattern... asks. The model's line becomes the one drill given every position, and the part is rebuilt. Places off the face or overlapping each other are refused with nothing cut. Hidden in 2D drafting. A part extruded from a Sketch works too when a circle inside its outline is the hole: the copies are written into that sketch as circles and the part is rebuilt; a circular pattern turns about the centre of another circle or arc of the sketch, the outline's by default, or a centre typed, and copies that would leave the outline or overlap are refused before anything is written.
Text...
Letters as a solid, text3d by name: the text, the bundled DejaVuSans (the default) or a font of the system's, the height of its capitals and its depth; with a planar face picked, raised on it or sunk its depth into it and cut, the part changing in place, and with nothing picked a part of its own on the XY, XZ or YZ plane. One undo entry. A font that is not found is refused.
Mate...
With two faces picked, the first on the part to move and the second on a part placed before it, place the one against the other: coincident, concentric (a hole's or a cylinder's wall picked), a distance or an angle. Writes mate into the model and runs it, as one undo entry; a mate the parts cannot meet with the mates before it is refused. The Parts dock's Mates row says what freedom a mated part has left.
Suggest Mates...
With a part picked, list the mates its features allow against the parts near it, best first: a cylinder to a hole it fits as concentric, opposed faces as coincident and as distance with the measured gap. Picking a row shows where the part would go. Check the ones to add and Accept Checked, or Accept All; each is written as its own mate and undo entry, and nothing is added without the accept. Ranked by how often you accepted the same kind of pair before. Moving a part near another says on the status bar that mates are suggested.
Edit Mate...
With a mate's row picked in the Feature Tree (also on that row's right-click menu, or a double click on it): change the mate's kind, and its value in mm or degrees, in the Edit Mate box. The new mate is written on the same line of the model and the model run, one step for Undo; a mate the model refuses leaves the model as it was. A mate made in a loop or from variables is not rewritten: the window names its line and shows it.
Delete Mate
With a mate's row picked in the Feature Tree (also on that row's right-click menu): take that mate's line out of the model and run it, one step for Undo. The part keeps its other mates.
Printability
Say whether the picked entry will print: its mass, its overhangs and its thinnest wall, in a box and in the output pane.
Show Overhangs
Tick to colour the picked entry's overhanging faces in the view; picking something else, or unticking, takes them down. A Run, undo or edit that changes the entry's shape colours the new faces.
Printing Material...

Bill of Materials...

Check Interference...

Import DXF...
Bring a DXF's profile into the model as a sketch: the Import wizard, from its first page, picks the file, the plane to draw it on, a scale and the layers. Its LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE (bulges as arcs) and POLYLINE entities are read on every layer, in millimetres by the file's $INSUNITS (millimetres when it says none), then scaled; ends within 1e-6 mm are joined, so each closed chain is a loop ready to extrude, a loop inside another a hole. The sketch is written into model.py as its own lines, named after the file (plate.dxf gives plate_dxf), so the file stays the model and the DXF is not needed again; the lines and the status bar say what the file held that is not read (text, dimensions, splines, blocks and the rest). A model can also call import_dxf(path, plane, scale=, offset=, layers=) itself.
Line
The drawing tool a sketch starts in: each click puts a point down, joined to the one before. Escape comes back to it from any tool, ending the figure being drawn. Return, a double click, Finish Figure or choosing a tool that draws a figure of its own ends the chain where it is, and the next click starts a new figure: a sketch holds many figures, open or closed. While a sketch is open the status bar reads where the pointer is on the sketch plane in millimetres, the snap firing there, and the measurement the live tool is waiting for: a line's length and angle, a rectangle's width and height, a circle's radius, an arc's radius and included angle, a polygon's across-flats and side, a slot's length and width, an ellipse's two half-axes. Typing a number instead of clicking opens a small entry beside the pointer for those measurements: Tab moves between the two, Return puts the point down at exactly that size and Escape goes back to clicking; lengths are millimetres and angles degrees. As each figure is finished the script pane shows it, written as sketch = (Sketch(...)...) after the model that was there, so the numbers can be read while drawing; Cancel Sketch takes the line out again, an extrude or revolve writes the part in its place, and typing in the pane while drawing leaves it to you. Anything the sketch refuses, a click it cannot draw, a corner too small for its fillet, an offset the shape cannot take, a constraint the others leave no room for, is shown in a box that says what was asked, why not and what would work, and the same words go to the output pane; the sketch is left as it was. The live tool is checked on the Sketch toolbar and named on the status bar, and a line from the last point follows the pointer.
Rectangle
Two clicks, one corner and then the opposite one, put down an axis-aligned rectangle as four points in a closed loop, ready to constrain or extrude. The outline follows the pointer after the first corner. It is a figure of its own, drawn beside whatever else the sketch holds.
Circle
Two clicks, the centre and then a point on the rim, put down a real circle, written into the model as one circle call. The rim follows the pointer after the centre, and the status bar reads the live radius. Circles are drawn beside whatever else is there: inside a closed outline they are holes, and on their own the largest is the outline. A rim on the centre draws nothing and says so.
Arc
A three-point arc in the chain being drawn: its start (the last point, or a first click on an empty sketch), its end, then a point on the arc. Three points in line draw a straight segment and say so. An end on the first point closes the loop.
Centre Arc
An arc about a centre, going anticlockwise: the centre, the start (the last point, or a click on an empty sketch), then the end, which lands on the circle towards the click. The status bar reads the radius. An end on the first point closes the loop.
Polygon
A regular polygon: the centre, then a corner on the circle around it. The number of sides, 3 to 24, is asked every time the tool is chosen, the last answer offered (6 the first time). The corners are points in a closed loop, ready to constrain or extrude. A figure of its own, beside the others.
Slot
Two centres, then a click as far from the line through them as half the slot is wide: two parallel sides capped by half circles, written into the model as one slot call. The status bar reads the width. A figure of its own, beside the others.
Ellipse
The centre, the end of the major axis, then a click as far from that axis as the minor half-axis is long: an exact ellipse, written into the model as one ellipse call. The status bar reads each half-axis as it is drawn. A figure of its own, beside the others.
Spline
A smooth curve through every point clicked, ended by a double click or Return. It is left open: Close Sketch joins its last point to its first with a straight line, when that is wanted. It needs three points at least; with fewer, Return says so and draws nothing. A figure of its own, beside the others.
Done with Line
Leave the live tool, as Escape does: the figure being drawn is ended where it is and Line is live again; Trim and Break are left without ending anything. The entry is named for the live tool ("Done with Break") and is first on the right-click menu while a sketch is open, where Cancel Sketch is last. Return does the same when no figure is under way; part way through one it ends the figure, as it always has. The status bar ends with what the live tool waits for and "Esc or Enter when done", and once figures are set aside it counts them and all their points ("7 figures, 14 points").
Finish Figure
End the figure being drawn where it is, open, and leave the sketch open for the next, as Return and a double click do; it is also on the right-click menu. Extrude and Revolve take every closed figure: side by side they are separate solids, and one inside another is a hole.
Close Sketch
Close the figure being drawn, so it can be extruded or revolved; the figures finished before it are left as they were.
Cancel Sketch
Throw the sketch away and leave the document as it was.
Horizontal...

Vertical...

Coincident...

Dimension...

Constraints...

Radius...

Diameter...
Fix a circle's diameter, as Radius does.
Tangent...
Make a segment's line, the one under the cursor or one asked for by number, touch a circle asked for by number. On a sketch with arcs, a straight segment or a circle is chosen, then a circle or an arc, so a line or a circle can touch an arc.
Concentric...
Give two circles, asked for by number, one centre; on a sketch with arcs, any two of its circles and arcs, chosen from a list.
Equal...
Make two segments the same length, or two circles or two arcs the same size, each chosen from a list. A constraint on circles or arcs that cannot be met is said in the status bar and changes nothing.
Fillet Corner...
Round a corner where two straight segments meet, the point under the cursor or one asked for by number, with an arc. The radius is asked every time, the last one offered (2.0 the first time). One too large for the corner is said in the status bar and changes nothing.
Chamfer Corner...
Cut a corner straight across, the same distance back along each side, picked as Fillet Corner picks. The distance is asked every time, the last one offered (2.0 the first time).
Offset...
Replace the closed sketch with its offset by a distance that is asked for, outwards, or inwards when negative, so a wall, a clearance or a gasket comes from a shape already drawn. Corners going outwards are rounded. After the distance it asks whether to keep the original, Keep both offered: kept, the offset and the original are the outline and the hole of one sketch, whichever is outside, so a gasket or a wall is one step; Replace swaps the loop for its offset. An inward offset the shape cannot take is said in the status bar and changes nothing.
Trim
A tool, like Line: while it is live the piece under the pointer lights up, and each click cuts the piece of line, arc, circle, ellipse or spline there back to where it next crosses another figure, or to its own end. A chain opens or comes apart there, a circle becomes the arc that is left and an ellipse the elliptical arc, and a slot is cut as its lines and caps. It stays live until another tool is chosen or Esc is pressed; a click on nothing, or on a piece that crosses nothing, says why in a box.
Mirror...
Copy figures across a line, keeping the originals or replacing them: every figure or one, across the X or Y axis of the sketch plane or any straight segment drawn.
Pattern...
Repeat a circle inside the outline of the sketch being drawn, as one sketch step: linear along the sketch's x or y, circular about the centre of another circle or arc or a centre typed, or a grid. Copies that would leave the outline, or overlap a hole or each other, are refused and nothing is drawn.
Linetype...
Draw figures in a linetype: every figure or one, continuous, dashed, centre or phantom, written as linetype= on the figure's call in the model. It changes how the figure is drawn and exported, not what an extrude or a revolve makes of it. Also on the right-click menu while sketching.
Break
A tool, like Trim: each click splits the line, arc or curve there in two at that place, keeping both; a closed loop or a whole ellipse opens there instead. A circle, which one cut leaves whole, is refused.
Extrude...
Extrude the closed sketch by a height that is asked for.
Revolve...
Revolve the closed sketch about an axis by an angle that is asked for. The axis is the sketch plane's own x axis, drawn in the view while the angle is asked. An outline with one straight side on the axis is turned into a solid with no hole; one that crosses the axis is refused, saying where: "the outline crosses the axis at (10, 0) and (0, 0)".
A sketch click snaps to what is within a few pixels of it, trying in order: a point already drawn, a straight segment's midpoint, an arc's or circle's centre, the nearest place on a straight segment, the sketch plane's own axes, and a grid whose spacing follows the zoom. A small mark at the pointer shows the snap that would fire. Hold Alt to snap to nothing.
A point already drawn can be dragged with the left button: it snaps as a click does, the constraints are solved again as it moves with every other point held, and a drag they will not allow leaves it where it was. One drag is one Undo. While a sketch is open, Delete (it reads Delete Segment) takes away the segment under the cursor: a closed loop opens there, and an open chain can lose either end segment. The picked parts are not touched.

Base Flange...
Make the closed sketch in hand, drawn with the line tool or as one rectangle with the rectangle tool, a sheet part: the outline a sheet's thickness thick, with each circle drawn wholly inside it cut through as a hole (an outline may hold arcs, as a slot's does, and one circle alone is a disc; no flange is bent on an arc, and the flat pattern keeps the arcs) and each rectangle drawn wholly inside it with the rectangle tool cut through as a cutout (cutouts= is written only when there are some), and each slot drawn wholly inside it with the slot tool cut through as a rounded slot, in any direction (slots= is written only when there are some). Flange...
Bend a flange on an edge of the picked sheet part. One dialog holds every choice: the edge (edge n runs from corner n to corner n + 1), from its list or by clicking it in the view, where the free edges are highlighted and the ones with a flange already are drawn grey and cannot be chosen, and after the outline's edges the list offers the edges of each flange already there, the two ends of its leg and its free edge, named as "Edge 3 leg, start end, 114 mm" and "Edge 3 return, free edge, 194 mm", each clicked in the view as the outline's are and written into the model as (3, 'start') or (3, 'free'); the length, and whether it runs to the leg or to the outside mould line (length_from="outside" is written only then); the angle (180 for an open hem); up or down; the flange's own bend radius (offered as the sheet's; bend_radius= is written only when it differs); how far in from the edge's start and end it begins and stops (0 for the full edge); whether to cut a bend relief slot beside each inset end; its return length, a second 90 degree bend at the leg's end and a return leg that long (0 for none; return_length= is written only when it is above 0); the holes through its leg, as one line u, v, d; u, v, d (u along the edge, v out from the bend, d the diameter; empty for none; holes= is written only when there are some); and the cutouts through its leg, as one line u, v, w, h; u, v, w, h (the centre's u and v as a hole's, w along the edge and h along the leg; empty for none; cutouts= is written only when there are some), and the rounded slots through its leg, as one line u1, v1, u2, v2, w; ... (the centres of each slot's two round ends, u and v as a hole's, and its width, in any direction; empty for none; slots= is written only when there are some; a line that is not groups of five numbers, or a slot that reaches the bend or meets a hole, keeps OK grey with its reason). Beside the fields a cross-section diagram shows what each means, the element of the field in focus highlighted. Each value is checked as it is typed, the reason beside its field; the view shows the flanged part faintly as it would be made; and OK is enabled only once it can be made, so nothing is refused after it. Every dialog of DX-CAD's own has a ? button beside its other buttons that opens the same topic as F1 does there. An add-on's dialogs are the add-on's own and have none.
In the help window, Back and Forward go through the pages looked at, Start goes to the first page, and a link opens the page it names; a link to a web address opens in your browser. The box at the top searches the topics, every heading of the guide and every command by the words typed, and Enter or a click opens the one picked. The window takes the light or the dark theme with the view, and it stays open while a dialog is.
A command that is carried out in steps has them at the top of its topic, a line each. Asked for while the command is under way, with F1 or ?, the help says which step you are on, marked, and the steps left: a line being drawn, a part being moved, a view being placed, a rectangle being dragged for Zoom Window. The commands a new user meets first also have a short animation of the command carried out on an example, shown above the page: it plays as the topic opens and goes round until Pause is pressed, and Play starts it again.
The panels
What each part of the window is, which is where F1 lands with the focus in it.
The 3D view
The document's parts, drawn by the OpenCASCADE viewer. A left drag orbits, a middle drag pans and the wheel zooms at the pointer; a click picks the part, face or edge under it, and Ctrl+click adds one to what is picked. File > Settings > Controls can make the middle button orbit instead. The view's right-click menu has the commands that act on what is picked. Fit, the seven views and the display modes are under View and on the View and Display toolbars.
The drawing sheet
A drawing tab shows its sheet in the view's place: the views, their sizes and labels, the title block and the parts list. A click selects a view and a drag moves it; the wheel zooms at the pointer and a middle drag pans, and View > Fit Sheet shows the whole sheet again. A right-click on a view or on the sheet has what can be changed there. With several sheets, the tabs along the bottom choose the one shown.
A view may be turned a quarter turn at a time about its own centre, which stays where it is: Rotate 90 Anticlockwise and Rotate 90 Clockwise on the view's right-click menu, or Rotation in Drawing properties, 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees anticlockwise. Its lines, hidden lines, centre lines and sizes turn with it; a size says what it said before, and the words and the view's label stay level. Each turn is one undo step, and the drawing keeps it when saved. A top or right view turned is no longer kept in line with the front, as one unlocked; turning the front turns only the front.
Every text of the title block, a field's value and a cell's caption alike, can be dragged to another place on the sheet, as a view is; only the text dragged moves while the pointer does. Each drag is one undo step, the drawing keeps how far each text was moved when saved, and the sheet, the DXF and the PDF draw it there. Reset Text Positions, on the title block's right-click menu, puts every text back where the template has it, as one undo step.
The Parts list
The Parts dock, on the left: the document's parts in the model's order, a sub-assembly's parts under it. A click on a row picks the part and puts the model pane on its line, and the eye beside a row hides or shows the part. Under the list are the picked part's properties: its name, volume, size, material, mass and colour. View > Parts shows or hides the dock.
The History list
The History tab beside Parts: every edit the undo history holds, oldest first, the current one marked. A click on an earlier entry undoes back to it, and on a later one redoes to it. View > History shows or hides it.
The Feature Tree
Each part in the order the model builds it and, beneath it, its features, its sketches and its mates. A click on a row picks the part and puts the model pane on that row's line. Nothing in the tree is dragged or re-ordered. View > Feature Tree opens and closes it. A double click on a flange's row, or Edit Flange... on its right-click menu, opens the Flange dialog on that flange. A mate's row has Edit Mate... and Delete Mate on its right-click menu, and a double click on it opens the Edit Mate box; neither moves a row.
The Parameters form
The model's named values as a form (View > Parameters). Each top-level NAME = value line of the model pane is a field, under the model's own comment headings; the comment on its line gives its unit, its range (# mm, 1200..4000) or its choices (# paint | galvanised | powder, or # "flat" or "pitched"). A unit word anywhere in the comment is the value's, unless it follows another number (# under the 4 mm lid is the lid's); a range counts in brackets of its own, (1..17), or as a clause of its own, never inside a sentence; choices may be named on the indented comment lines just below the value. A tuple of numbers is a field per member, X_DOOR[0] and X_DOOR[1], and A, B = 80, 50 a field per name. Private names (a leading underscore), names DX-CAD gives every model, and tables holding text are left out. Type a value and press Enter, tick a box or pick a choice: only that value is written into the model, the model is rebuilt, and one Undo takes both back. A value out of its range, or not a number where one is wanted, is refused at the top of the form and on the status bar, and nothing changes. A value worked out from others is shown with its expression and cannot be typed into: change the values it is made from. The form holds no rules between values: it is the model's own values, nothing more. An agent reads and sets the same values with the get_parameters and set_parameter tools.
The output pane
Under the model pane: what the last run printed, and what a command refused and why. View > Output shows or hides it.
The Assistant
The Assistant dock, along the bottom of the view: type a request and the steps taken to build or change the document show in the chat, each one written into the model and one Undo. Stop ends a turn. View > Assistant, or Ctrl+Shift+A, shows or hides it, and File > Settings > Assistant chooses the provider and its model.
Each request carries model.py whole, as far as the provider has room for it: 200,000 characters to Claude (your own Anthropic key or the DX-CAD account), 100,000 to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and Gemini, and 24,000 to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or two characters for each token of its Context size (tokens) in Settings > Assistant where you give it. A longer script is cut at the end of a line, and the request says after which line it was cut.
Drawing properties
While a drawing tab is in front, the left dock shows the sheet's size, its Title Block..., the parts list's columns and, for the view clicked on the sheet, its label, its scale and its hidden lines.
A new view's hidden lines are off: tick Hidden lines to show that view's, a view Add View put there as much as one of the sheet's four. Leave out small parts, with a size in mm, leaves the parts whose largest size is under it out of that view's lines only; the other views, the view's sizes and the parts list are as they were.
A new drawing's centre marks, the two centre lines across each hole a view sees round, are off, unless its model calls centre_marks(True). Centre marks under the sheet turns them on or off for the whole drawing, and Centre marks under the view clicked for that view alone, over the drawing's; each is one undo entry and the .dxcdrg keeps both. A drawing saved before them opens with them on.
Line type is the type Drawing > Line and Polyline draw with: Thin, Thick, Centre or Hidden. The drawing's file keeps it, and a change is one undo step; a line already drawn keeps its own type, changed on its right-click menu.
Text height is the height the drawing letters in: Sheet's own, 2.5, 3.5, 5 or 7 mm. The views' labels, the title block's fields, the dimensions and an add-on's annotations take it; the drawing's file keeps it, and a change is one undo step.
Dimensions sets how the drawing's dimensions are drawn, each in the sheet's millimetres: Arrow size (0.5 to 10), Text height (2.5, 3.5, 5 or 7, over the drawing's), Text gap from the line (0.2 to 5), First line from the view and Spacing between lines (2 to 40 each), and Extension line gap (0 to 5) and overshoot (0 to 10). A field left empty is the sheet's own, which it shows greyed; a value outside its range is refused in words on the status bar. Each change is one undo step, the drawing's file keeps it and the DXF's DXCAD dimension style carries it. The sheet's own sizes, hole callouts and HOLES NOT DIMENSIONED note stand clear of the views' lines, by their text's real height, and every dimension's text stands the gap off its line; a dimension an add-on placed stays where it was put. Settings > Drawings holds the style a new drawing starts with.
Make Dimensions Editable, on a view's right-click menu for that view or on the sheet's for every view, makes the sheet's own sizes, hole callouts and HOLES NOT DIMENSIONED note the drawing's own, where they stand and saying what they said, as one undo step; the sheet then draws none of its own for that view. Each is then selected by a click, moved by its handle, edited by a double-click (a value typed over the one measured, which is marked as typed, and a tolerance after it; an empty value gives the measured one back) and taken off by Delete, one undo step each, nothing else on the sheet moving. Their values are measured from the model whenever the sheet is drawn, so a change of the model updates them; the drawing's file keeps them, and the PDF and DXF carry them. A drawing never asked draws as it did.

A large view shows at once as its outline, every edge seen straight through, and its lines, with what is hidden taken out, come in behind while the window stays free; the status bar says how many views are still being worked out.
