The Animate box
View > Animate...: a short video of the model, from the view on screen, in the window's theme. Pick one of the three choices, Explode and back, Turn around or Build it up; tick and turn while it moves for a turn as well (Turn around is a turn already); choose the Length, 3 to 30 seconds, the Size, Video 720p (1280 x 720), Video 1080p (1920 x 1080), Square (1080 x 1080) or Small GIF, and the Format. MP4 (H.264) is greyed, with the reason beside it, where this machine has no H.264 encoder, and for Small GIF; a GIF is drawn at most 800 pixels wide, 15 frames a second. Type a Title for a two-second card with it at the start, or leave it empty for none; the title is not kept for the next time. Build it up names each part as it arrives. Preview plays the animation small in the box, looping, as it will be saved, and Stop or any change of choice stops it. Save... closes the box, asks for the file and writes it under a bar with Cancel; Cancel stops it part way and leaves no file. Close shuts the box. The box keeps what it was last given for the next time. The three recipes, the sizes and the formats, with a GIF of each, are in Animations.
The Bill of Materials box
Model > Bill of Materials...: the parts as lines, with how many of each, volume, mass and size. Save CSV... writes the same table to a file; Close shuts the box and changes nothing.
The command search
Help > Search Commands..., or Ctrl+K: type part of a command's name, or of another name it commonly goes by, and the list narrows to the commands that can be used now. Enter or a double click runs the one picked; Esc leaves without running anything.
The error box
Shown when something went wrong that DX-CAD did not expect: one line saying what happened, with the whole story in the log. Copy Details puts the version, the platform and the error on the clipboard, Open Log Folder opens where the log is kept, and Continue closes the box; the window carries on.
The Flange dialog
Sheet Metal > Flange...: every choice of a flange on an edge of the picked sheet part, the edge, the length, the angle, up or down, the bend radius, the insets, the reliefs, the return, and the holes, cutouts and rounded slots through its leg; the diagram's legend says the leg takes all three. Each value is checked as it is typed, with the reason beside its field, the picture beside the fields shows what the field in focus means, and the view shows the part faintly as it would be made. OK is enabled only when the flange can be made. The Edge list holds the outline's edges and then the edges of the flanges already there: the two ends of each one's leg and its free edge, so a part with a flange on every edge of its base can take more. On one of those Direction reads "towards the inside", the side that flange's own bend has its inside, and "outward", and relief is refused. F1 shows the command's steps, the one in hand marked. The corner post of the tutorial is built with this dialog alone. Return angle and Return turns bend a return its own way: any angle above 0 and below 180, turned in, back over the base, or out, away from it; they are read only when Return length is above 0. Hem makes the flange a hem by name: closed, the leg folded flat onto the base, or teardrop, bent past 180 round Teardrop radius until its free edge comes down to the base. While one is chosen Angle and Bend radius are grey, since a hem has its own, and Teardrop radius is read for a teardrop alone; an open hem is still Angle 180 with Hem left at none.
All edges puts a flange on every free edge of the outline in one go. Ticked, a table opens under the fields with a row for each of those edges: the edge, then its Length, Length to, Angle, Direction, Bend radius, Return length, Start inset, End inset and Corners. Every row starts with the fields' values as they stood and is then its own; a number is typed in its cell and a choice made in its list. A row whose edge is unticked gets no flange. The flanges are made in the rows' order and are one undo step. A table's flanges take no relief, holes or cutouts: those are given to one flange, with the box unticked.
When a value is wrong the dialog says which edge, which value and why, as "Edge 2: Angle 200: an angle is above 0 and at most 180." When each value is right in itself but the flange would run into the part, it names the length to shorten, the return first and then the leg, and the longest that works there, which it finds by making the flange shorter.
Edit Flange changes a flange the model already has. Double-click the flange's row in the Feature tree, or right-click it and choose Edit Flange...: the dialog opens with the values the flange was written with, its edge kept. OK writes the flange() call again and builds the part from that flange on, everything made after it included, as one undo step. The view shows nothing of the edit until then. A flange whose values the model works out, from a variable or a loop, is changed in the model pane, which is put on its line; an edit after which a later step no longer builds is refused with that step's reason, and nothing changes.
The Base Flange dialog
Sheet Metal > Base Flange...: the material and a stocked gauge of it, or Custom with the thickness, the bend radius and the K-factor, for the sheet part made from the closed sketch in hand. Each number is checked as it is typed, and OK is enabled only when the part can be made.
The Check Interference box
Model > Check Interference...: the pairs of parts that overlap, each with the volume they share. The overlaps show in red in the view until the box is closed. "Also list pairs closer than [ ] mm", empty to begin with: type a gap and press Enter or List, and every pair that does not overlap and is nearer than that is listed after the overlaps, with its gap to three places and its two nearest points, and a red line is drawn between those points until the box is closed. Touching faces read 0.000. Empty, the box lists what it always did.
The Licences box
Help > Licences...: the third-party notices as this copy of DX-CAD ships them, every library it runs on with its version and licence, and the LGPL texts in full.
The Licence box
Help > Licence...: where this install's licence stands. Type a licence key and press Activate, or sign in with the email address the licence was bought with: Send code, then the six digits from the email and Sign in. Deactivate gives the seat back for another computer. The box shows the install id a seat is counted by.
Licences go on sale on 1 November 2026, or the day the release's latest.json names. Until that day, Activate, Send code and Sign in contact nothing: each says, in a box titled "Licences from 1 November 2026", that licences (a paid subscription) are available from that day, and that DX-CAD and its add-ons cost nothing until your trial ends. Until then the box and the trial's notices say "Licences are available from 1 November 2026." where they would give a link to buy one. The box says each date once: one line for DX-CAD's trial (the days left, its last day and the day editing and saving lock without a licence) and one for the add-ons, "Free during your 30-day trial (ends DATE)", which lock with editing unless a licence names them; it grows to show every line in full, also after an answer. Deactivate is greyed unless a licence is activated on this computer. When the licence service cannot be reached, it says only "DX-CAD could not reach the licence service. Check your internet connection and try again."; what went wrong is written to DX-CAD's log, with no key, code, email or token in it. latest.json may also name a day no trial ends before (its trial_until): a trial that would end sooner then locks at 23:59 UK time on that day, and the box and the notices say that day.
An activated licence is checked online at least every 14 days: at each start and every 8 hours while DX-CAD is open, the status bar saying "Checking the licence..." at a start that needs it until the answer comes. If it could not be (the computer offline that long, or the clock set back past the last check), the box, the status bar and the command line say "Your licence could not be checked online in the last 14 days", not that a trial has ended; the next start with the network back checks it again with nothing typed, and the key box holds the key last used, ready to activate again.
DX-CAD keeps the latest date and time it has seen on this computer, a moment and nothing else, and never moves it back. If the computer's clock is set more than a day before it and no licence is active, the box and the status bar say "The computer's clock is set earlier than the last time DX-CAD ran", with that day, and editing and saving wait until the clock is set right; opening, viewing and exporting still work. This keeps a clock set back from reopening a trial that has ended. It never locks before that day has really passed, so never during the trial, which lets everyone edit whatever the clock says, and never with a licence active, whose add-ons stay granted too; a clock that jumps more than two days ahead is not believed until a server's date agrees, so a clock set ahead by mistake and set right again locks nothing; and a server's date wins over the computer's. When DX-CAD has asked the network anyway (the update check, the licence service), it compares the computer's clock with the server's: more than an hour apart, the box says so ("Your computer's clock is 3 hours behind the server's"), and a server more than a day ahead counts as the latest time seen. Nothing locks on the gap alone.
An add-on's panel
A greyed command of an add-on that is not installed opens a short panel: the command, the add-on it belongs to and what the add-on adds, with a Buy button that opens the add-on's page in your browser. Nothing is run and nothing is sent.
The Add Part Sheets box
Drawing > Add Part Sheets...: the model's sub-assemblies and parts, each with a tick box, none ticked. Tick the ones that are to have a sheet of their own and press Make Sheets; Cancel adds nothing. The sheets are made five at a time, with a question after each five.
The search field above the list narrows it as you type: any part of the name, upper or lower case alike. A part the search hides keeps its tick, and gets its sheet. Tick all shown and Untick all shown tick or untick the parts listed and no other; "N ticked" beside Make Sheets counts every tick, shown or not. Enter in the search field does not make the sheets.
"Show the flat pattern on sheet metal parts' sheets", ticked at first, gives the sheet of each sheet metal part a fifth view, its flat pattern; with it off the sheets are made with their four views alone.
The recovery box
Shown at the start when DX-CAD did not close cleanly: the tabs that had changes not saved, each by its name and when it was kept. Recover opens every one as a tab with its changes, Discard throws them away, and Later leaves them for the next start.
The Settings dialog
File > Settings...: the settings in groups. Mode is 2D drafting or 3D modelling; View holds Show Planes; Runs, the seconds a run of the model is given, and whether Claude may run models from Claude Desktop (trusted projects only), the question Connect Claude Desktop asks once; Recovery, the minutes between keeps of the unsaved tabs; Parts, the default material; Drawings, the number of parts above which a new drawing asks to be laid out for speed and the dimension style a new drawing starts with; Updates, whether to check at the start; Controls, DX-CAD's own mouse and keys or the classic CAD controls; and Assistant, its provider, model and address. OK keeps the changes and Cancel leaves everything as it was. View's Toolbars... button opens the Toolbars box, whose OK shows and hides the toolbars at once.
The Keyboard Shortcuts box
Help > Keyboard Shortcuts: every action that has a shortcut, by menu, action and keys, read from the window's own actions. The box at the top searches actions and keys.
The Suggest Mates box
Model > Suggest Mates...: the mates the picked part's features allow against the parts near it, best first. Picking a row shows where the part would go. Tick the ones to add and press Accept Checked, or Accept All; Cancel adds none.
The Import wizard
File > Import..., or Sketch > Import DXF...: a STEP file or a DXF drawing brought in in four steps, Back and Cancel on each. 1. The file: typed, or found with Browse...; its format is read from what it holds, not its name, so a DXF named .step is read as DXF. A DWG is refused, and Next stays off: DX-CAD does not read DWG yet, so save it as DXF from the program that made it. 2. Check, adding nothing: for STEP the units the file declares, its solids, shells and faces, the names and colours it carries, how many solids are valid, its open shells and its size, with a warning when it is under 1 mm or over 100 m across, which looks like a units mistake; for DXF its units, its layers with the lines, arcs and circles on each, the closed loops, what will be left out and its extents. 3. Place: STEP as one part or a part per solid, named from the file, its scale and the units to read it in where the file says the wrong ones; DXF on which plane, its scale and which layers. 4. Summary of what Finish adds. Finish writes it into the model (import_step, or the DXF's sketch as its own lines) and runs it, one step for Undo; Cancel adds nothing. After a DXF the window works in 2D drafting, and a STEP brought in while in 2D drafting turns it to 3D modelling; the status bar says so. Nothing is previewed: the parts appear after Finish.
The Edit Mate box
Model > Edit Mate..., or a mate's row in the Feature tree right-clicked or double-clicked: the two parts and the face, hole or plane each names, shown and not changed here; the kind; and the value, in mm for a distance and degrees for an angle, greyed for coincident and concentric. OK writes the new mate on the same line of the model and runs it, one step for Undo; Cancel changes nothing. There is no preview: the parts move after OK. To mate other faces, use Delete Mate, then Mate... or Suggest Mates....
The Title Block dialog
File > Title Block...: the fields filled in once for every drawing, company, drawn by, checked by, material, finish, general tolerance, drawing number and revision, and the font and height the drawing is lettered in. OK keeps them for every drawing made after; Cancel leaves them as they were.
Every text a title block shows has a line (item 974), the ones the sheet fills itself too: title, model, scale, size, sheet and date, and the default sheets' customer, project, drawing type and status, manufacturing order number, copyright statement, sheet count and revision table. A text the sheet fills itself shows what it fills it with, greyed, as its hint: left blank it stays automatic, typed it is used instead. File > Title Block... lists every sheet's texts, as defaults for each new drawing; the Title Block... button in Drawing properties lists the texts of the drawing in front's own sheet, kept in its .dxcdrg, and OK there is one undo step. The lines scroll; the font, the text height, OK and Cancel stay in view.
A value in the title block can be changed where it stands: double-click it on the sheet and a box opens over it, holding what it shows. Enter keeps what is typed, one undo step; Escape, or a click elsewhere, leaves it. A value the sheet fills itself says so in the box, "Automatic: ...", and may be typed over; clearing the box gives the automatic value back. The title block's right-click menu has Edit Title Block... for every field at once, beside Reset Text Positions.
The Toolbars box
View > Toolbars..., or the Toolbars... button in File > Settings: every toolbar the window has, the add-ons' too, in the order they stand, ticked if it is shown. Show All ticks every one and Hide All unticks them; OK shows and hides them together and keeps the choice for the next start, and Cancel leaves them as they were.
The Version History box
File > Version History...: the model's versions, newest first, each with its time, who made it and what changed. Choosing one shows, as text, the lines taken out (-) and put in (+) from it to the script in the pane; there is no 3D preview. Restore puts it in the pane and builds it, as one undo step, and keeps it as a new version; Save as .py... writes its text to a file; Close changes nothing. An agent lists them with list_versions and restores one with restore_version.
The What's New box
Shown once after an update: what changed in the version now installed, as its release notes say it. Close shuts it.
Keyboard shortcuts
Every action that has a shortcut, as Help > Keyboard Shortcuts lists it. The table is written by python -m dxcad.docsgen shortcuts from the window's own actions, and a test fails if it drifts. Ctrl is Cmd on a Mac.

The model pane
The pane on the right is the model.py, and it is the document's source of truth: the shapes in the scene are what the last run of that text built. Typing in it changes nothing until the model is run.
Run Script, or F5, runs it. What it prints goes to the output pane, and a model that raises puts the cursor on the line that raised, with the helper file's own line above it when the failure was in a file beside the model.
Run on Change watches the model.py on disk, and its helpers, and runs the model again whenever one of them is saved. It is for an editor in another window: the pane follows the file rather than the other way round. It is off for every new window and is taken off again by New and by Open.
No Time Limit lifts the limit a run is given, a minute unless Settings > Runs sets another, from 5 s to an hour. A run happens on the window's own thread, so a model that never ends is a window that never answers again; the limit is there so that a typo costs a minute rather than everything typed since the last save. A run or a check the limit stops says so in one sentence, on the status line, in the output pane and in Copy Details alike ("Stopped at the 60 s time limit; Model > No Time Limit lifts it"), with no trace and no line of the model marked, and the document is as it was before the run. The tick is remembered from one session to the next, and stays through New, Open and a change of tab; an agent's run in the window is held to the same limit.
Check Model runs the model and says what it would change without changing anything, and Show in Script goes the other way, from a part in the scene to the line that built it.
Adopt Parts is for a document holding parts no model builds, which is what an older project looks like: it writes each of them to a file beside the project and adds the line that reads it back, so the model builds everything again.
The model a project carries
A part or assembly file is something people are sent, and the model inside one is a program. So a project opened from a file is asked about before its model is run for the first time, by Run, by F5 or by Run on Change: the question says that a model is Python and runs with your own permissions, and names the project. Answering no runs nothing and changes nothing. Answering yes runs it, and the window does not ask again until it is given another project.
A model you opened by name, one you typed into a new project and one the window wrote itself are your own and are never asked about.
Whether any of this looks right on a desktop is a manual check: the suite drives the window offscreen, where nothing is drawn. The scene itself, the orbiting and the picking, is the one part of DX-CAD no test can see.

DX-CAD documentation
Known limitations
DX-CAD™ builds every solid with OpenCASCADE (OCCT), the geometry kernel underneath it; its release notes are at github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/releases. This page says plainly what DX-CAD cannot do, or does unreliably, why, and what to do instead. It describes the version you have and promises nothing about later ones. At the end, every case of DX-CAD's robustness suite is listed with what it comes to today, regenerated from the suite itself.
In the diagrams, green is what works and red dashed is what is refused or goes wrong.
On this page
Fillets that would consume a face
Fillets meeting at a vertex
Variable-radius fillets
Booleans on coincident or tangent faces
Shelling and offsets on complex faces
Persistent naming
STEP and IGES files that need healing
No simultaneous assembly solver
Large assemblies
Pictures without a window on macOS
The robustness suite
Fillets that would consume a face
(Picture: Two 100 mm blocks from the front: 40 mm fillets on the top edges leave a flat top, valid; 50 mm fillets meet in the middle and take the whole top face, refused.)
Cause: a fillet as big as half the face it runs along leaves nothing of that face between its blends, and OCCT cannot build the solid that would need. DX-CAD refuses it and names the radius.
Workaround: make the fillet smaller than half the shortest edge it meets, or remove the face first and model the round as a revolve or a sketch arc.
Fillets meeting at a vertex
(Picture: A 10 mm cube from above: 4 mm fillets on every edge leave flat faces, valid; 5 mm fillets make the blends meet in a point, refused.)
Cause: where three or more filleted edges meet at a corner, OCCT has to build a corner patch between the blends. When the blends meet in a point, or nearly so, there is no patch to build, and the fillet fails.
Workaround: give a radius under half the shortest edge that meets the corner, or fillet fewer edges in one call; or chamfer the corner instead.
Variable-radius fillets
(Picture: One edge side on: a fillet of one radius along the whole edge, valid; a fillet growing from 2 mm to 8 mm, not offered.)
Cause: DX-CAD's fillets take one radius per call, from the model language, the window and the agent door alike; a blend whose radius changes along its edge is not offered.
Workaround: split the edge where the radius should change and fillet each part at its own radius, or model the shape as a loft between sketched sections.
Booleans on coincident or tangent faces
(Picture: Two blocks sharing a face: a hairline gap makes the fuse fail, red dashed; after the retry with a tolerance of 0.00001 mm, one clean solid, green.)
Cause: when two parts share a face, or touch along a line or at a point, floating-point noise can leave a hairline gap or overlap that OCCT reads as two solids. DX-CAD retries a failed boolean once with a fuzzy tolerance of 0.00001 mm (BOOLEAN_FUZZY_VALUE), which closes such gaps; when that fails too, or the parts only touch along a line or at a point, the boolean is refused rather than leaving two solids or an invalid one.
Workaround: make the parts overlap by some volume, at least a few hundredths of a millimetre, rather than only touching.
Shelling and offsets on complex faces
(Picture: A plate with a boss, cut through: a 1 mm wall fits inside the boss, valid; a 3 mm wall is wider than half the boss, so the walls cross, refused.)
Cause: hollowing a part offsets every face inwards by the wall's thickness. Where a feature is thinner than two walls, or a face is a free-form surface whose offset folds over itself, the offset faces cross and OCCT cannot close the shell.
Workaround: give a wall thinner than half the thinnest feature, or hollow the plain body first and add the thin features after.
Persistent naming
(Picture: A plate with one hole, then with a second hole added: the kernel's face 7 moves to the new hole, red dashed; DX-CAD's hole 1 stays on the first, green.)
Cause: OCCT numbers a solid's faces and edges afresh each time it is built, so "face 7" can be a different face after an earlier feature changes. This is the persistent naming problem every CAD kernel has.
Workaround: DX-CAD does not keep kernel numbers between runs. A model is a script, so each feature is built from the values in it, not from picked faces; mates and references name faces by what they are and where they lie ("hole 1", ">Z", a face picked by position), found again on every run; and each part keeps a stable id of its own in the file, whatever it is renamed. Name faces in a model by position, not by number.
STEP and IGES files that need healing
(Picture: A face read from a STEP file whose boundary does not close, red dashed, not a valid solid; the same face healed and closed, green.)
Cause: a STEP file from another program can carry faces whose edges do not quite meet, or solids that are not closed. DX-CAD reads STEP as it is and does not heal it, so such a solid is reported as not valid by OCCT's check, and booleans on it may fail. IGES files are not read at all.
Workaround: heal or sew the model in the program that wrote it and export it again as closed solids, in STEP (AP214 or AP242).
No simultaneous assembly solver
(Picture: Three parts: B placed against A by mate 1, then C against B by mate 2, green; a mate from C back to A closes a loop, red dashed, refused.)
Cause: DX-CAD resolves an assembly's mates one at a time, in the order the model writes them, each placing its part against parts already placed. A mate that would need several parts moved at once, such as one closing a loop, or one that disagrees with the mates before it, is refused rather than solved.
Workaround: write the mates in the order the parts are placed, each part mated to parts before it, and change the order by editing the script.
Large assemblies
(Picture: An assembly of a few dozen parts, quick, green; thousands of parts, each its own shape in the view, slow, red dashed.)
Cause: every part is its own full shape in the view and in the file, with no lightweight stand-ins, so an assembly of thousands of parts is slow to open, to turn and to save.
Workaround: keep sub-assemblies in files of their own and bring them in with use(), working on one at a time.
Pictures without a window on macOS
(Picture: A part's picture drawn with no window open: drawn on Windows and on Linux with a display, green; on macOS the request is refused, red dashed.)
Cause: a picture drawn with no window open (dxcad render, the agent's render_view, the gallery, and the preview a saved part carries for Explorer) needs a hidden native window for OCCT to draw into. On macOS that is a Cocoa window, made on the application's main thread, which DX-CAD does not make without its own window. Such a request is refused there, saying so, and a part saved on macOS has no preview picture.
Workaround: open the part in DX-CAD's window to see it, or draw its picture on Windows or on Linux. With the window open, the Assistant's render_view and the window link's draw from the window's own view on every platform (item 771), so the Assistant looks at the model on a Mac as it does elsewhere; only a picture asked for with no window open is refused there.
The robustness suite
The hard cases DX-CAD is tested against each time, each run as a model.py: booleans of coplanar and tangent faces, blends bigger than their edges allow, shells against what they meet, overlapping patterns, sheet bends of radius 0, tiny text and mates that cannot be met. Each ends in a valid solid or is refused with its reason and what would work instead, never a crash. This list is rewritten by python -m dxcad.docsgen limitations, and the test suite fails when it and the cases disagree.
Run on OCCT 7.9.3, each case a model.py as dxcad run runs one.

a mate to a hole the part has not got
refused
'hole 1': the part has 0 holes. What would work: name a hole the part has: 'hole 1' asks past its 0 holes, counted as dxcad describe lists them
a mate against the one before it
refused
mate('b', '<Z', 'p', '<Z', 'coincident') disagrees with the mates before it: it misses by 180 degrees. What would work: drop or change this mate, or one before it: the mates before it already hold the part, and this one misses by 180 degrees
an angle the mates before it rule out
refused
mate('b', '>X', 'p', '>Z', 'angle', 45) disagrees with the mates before it: it misses by 45 degrees. What would work: drop or change this mate, or one before it: the mates before it already hold the part, and this one misses by 45 degrees
a mate to a part placed after
refused
mate('b', '<Z', 'p', '>Z', 'coincident'): 'p' is placed after 'b'; a part is mated to parts placed before it. What would work: register 'p' before the part mated to it, and mate to parts placed earlier
a plane past the last one
refused
'<Z 3': 1 plane faces -Z, at z = 0. What would work: name a plane the part has facing -Z,: '<Z 3' is past the last one, as dxcad describe lists them

What is in DX-CAD, and what Drafting Pro adds
In DX-CAD itself. Drawing documents, title blocks and parts lists, to PDF and DXF.
In Drafting Pro. Dimensions, balloons, hole tables, tolerances and GD&T, section, detail and exploded views, revision tables and notes.
Its commands
These are the commands of Drafting Pro, as DX-CAD lists them in its menus and in command search:
Dimensions - Drafting Pro: Place dimensions on a drawing's views by picking edges and points.
Balloons - Drafting Pro: Number the parts on a drawing with balloons that match its parts list.
Hole tables - Drafting Pro: List a view's holes in a table, with their positions and sizes.
Tolerances - Drafting Pro: Give a dimension its limits or fits.
GD&T frames and datums - Drafting Pro: Add geometric tolerance frames and datum symbols.
Surface texture and weld symbols - Drafting Pro: Add surface texture and weld symbols to a drawing.
Revision table and notes - Drafting Pro: Keep a drawing's revisions in a table, and its general notes.
Automatic dimensioning and ballooning - Drafting Pro: Dimension and balloon a drawing's views in one step.
Section view - Drafting Pro: A drawing view cut along a line through the part.
Detail view - Drafting Pro: An enlarged view of part of another view.
Shaded view - Drafting Pro: A drawing view shaded as the 3D view shows the part.
Exploded view - Drafting Pro: A drawing view of an assembly with its parts drawn apart.
Trial and licence

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""A lipped channel, its width, depth and lips dimensioned to the outside.
A drawing gives a channel's sizes over the outside of the sheet, and
`length_from="outside"` takes a flange's length that way: the depth runs
outside to outside over both bends, and the lip to the outside at its own
bend. The base is drawn to where the bends start, the outside width less one
outside setback (bend radius plus thickness, at 90 degrees) at each side. A
slot runs across the bend of one side, given on the flat and cut as it will
be on the shop floor, on the flat and then bent: `bend_cut` wraps it round
the bend. Its flat is 196.096 x 30.000 mm. Build it and unfold it with:
dxcad run channel.py --output channel.dxcprt
dxcad flat channel.dxcprt --part channel
Tags: sheet
"""
WIDTH = 100.0
DEPTH = 40.0
LIP = 15.0
LENGTH = 30.0
THICKNESS = 2.0
BEND_RADIUS = 2.0
K_FACTOR = 0.44
SLOT_WIDTH = 6.0
spec = SheetSpec(THICKNESS, BEND_RADIUS, K_FACTOR)
setback = BEND_RADIUS + THICKNESS
inside = WIDTH - 2 * setback
channel = base_flange([(0, 0), (inside, 0), (inside, LENGTH), (0, LENGTH)], spec)
for edge in (1, 3):
channel = flange(channel, edge, DEPTH, return_length=LIP, length_from="outside")
# On the flat, edge 1's bend starts at x = inside: the slot runs from the base,
# over the bend, onto the leg.
channel = bend_cut(channel, slot=(inside - 6, LENGTH / 2, inside + 10, LENGTH / 2, SLOT_WIDTH))
part("channel", channel, color="galvanised")

"""A box and its lid, two parts from one model.
The box is a block hollowed to one wall thickness with its top left open. The
lid is a plate with a lip underneath that drops inside the walls with
CLEARANCE to spare all round. They fit because they are made from the same
numbers: change WALL and both parts change, and they fit still.

LENGTH = 100.0

HEIGHT = 40.0

LID = 3.0
LIP = 4.0

"""A bent handle, a round bar swept along a path.
Extrude carries a section in a straight line, revolve turns one about an axis
and loft runs between two of them; a section carried along a path the model
draws is a sweep. The path is an open wire, which is what Sketch.path() hands
back: two straight legs and a quarter turn between them, tangent to both, so
the bar bends rather than kinks. The section is a circle on the plane the
path sets off through.
Tags: sketch
"""
SECTION = 12.0
RUN = 40.0
BEND = 20.0
RISE = 30.0

# of the run. A positive radius turns left, and this one is a quarter circle:
# the corner it turns is BEND across and BEND up.

Sketch()
.move_to((0, 0))
.line_to((RUN, 0))
.arc_to((RUN + BEND, BEND), BEND)
.line_to((RUN + BEND, BEND + RISE))
)

part("handle", sweep(section.face(), path.path()), color="navy")

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""A 1000 x 800 cabinet door bent from 2 mm steel, its return lips mitred at the corners.
1000 x 800 overall, as a drawing gives it: a 45 mm flange on every edge,
each with a 25 mm return lip, both measured to the outside, bent with a
2 mm inside radius. Where two lips meet at a corner they are mitred, cut
back at 45 degrees with a 2 mm gap between them, so no lip runs into the
next. The base is the overall size less a bend radius and a thickness each
side, 992 x 792. Each 45 mm flange with its return is a 37 mm leg and a
21 mm lip, once both bends' setbacks (2 + 2 = 4 each) are taken off, and
each bend allows pi / 2 x (2 + 0.44 x 2) = 4.52389 mm, so every side of the
flat reaches 2 x 4.52389 + 37 + 21 = 67.04779 mm past the base. Its flat is
1126.096 x 926.096 mm, with eight bend lines and the mitres cut in its
corners.
dxcad run mitred_door.py --output mitred_door.dxcprt
dxcad flat mitred_door.dxcprt --part door
Tags: sheet
"""
WIDTH = 1000.0
HEIGHT = 800.0
FLANGE = 45.0
RETURN = 25.0
THICKNESS = 2.0
BEND_RADIUS = 2.0
K_FACTOR = 0.44
spec = SheetSpec(THICKNESS, BEND_RADIUS, K_FACTOR)
out = BEND_RADIUS + THICKNESS
base_x, base_y = WIDTH - 2 * out, HEIGHT - 2 * out
door = base_flange([(0, 0), (base_x, 0), (base_x, base_y), (0, base_y)], spec)
for edge in range(4):
door = flange(
door,
edge,
FLANGE,
return_length=RETURN,
length_from="outside",
corner_treatment="mitre",
)
part("door", door, color="galvanised")

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""A shaft in a housing with two collars and a cover, at fits of 0.05 to 0.2 mm.
The shaft runs in the housing's bore with FIT all round, each collar holds the
shaft with COLLAR_FIT all round, the lower collar stands GAP under the housing
and the cover GAP off its side. The upper collar is meant to stand just clear
of the housing's top, but STOP is -0.05: it runs 0.05 mm into it. Model >
Check Interference... finds that overlap, and "Also list pairs closer than
0.25 mm" lists the tight gaps with the overlap; set STOP = 0.1 to mend it.
Tags: assembly
"""
FIT = 0.1 # the bore's clearance round the shaft, mm
COLLAR_FIT = 0.05 # each collar's clearance round the shaft, mm
GAP = 0.2 # the lower collar under the housing, and the cover off its side, mm
STOP = -0.05 # the upper collar over the housing's top, mm: below 0 runs into it
SHAFT = 10.0 # the shaft's radius
LENGTH = 80.0 # the shaft's length
BLOCK = 40.0 # the housing, a cube
BOTTOM = 20.0 # the housing's underside, above the shaft's lower end
COLLAR = 16.0 # a collar's outer radius
COLLAR_LENGTH = 8.0
AXIS = (BLOCK / 2, BLOCK / 2)
bore = make_cylinder(SHAFT + FIT, BLOCK + 2, (*AXIS, BOTTOM - 1))
part("housing", cut(make_box(BLOCK, BLOCK, BLOCK, (0, 0, BOTTOM)), bore), color="steel")
part("shaft", make_cylinder(SHAFT, LENGTH, (*AXIS, 0)), color="hardware")
low = BOTTOM - GAP - COLLAR_LENGTH
high = BOTTOM + BLOCK + STOP
for name, z in (("collar_low", low), ("collar_high", high)):
ring = make_cylinder(COLLAR, COLLAR_LENGTH, (*AXIS, z))
hole = make_cylinder(SHAFT + COLLAR_FIT, COLLAR_LENGTH + 2, (*AXIS, z - 1))
part(name, cut(ring, hole), color="brass")
part("cover", make_box(5, BLOCK, BLOCK, (BLOCK + GAP, 0, BOTTOM)), color="navy")

text:
Questions and answers
What DX-CAD does and what it does not do, in plain words. Each answer is taken from the public documentation, and its link goes to the page that says more.
What DX-CAD does
What is the window, and how do I open it?
dxcad gui opens the viewer: an OpenCASCADE scene on the left, the model.py in a pane on the right, and the output of the last run under it.
More: The window
Does DX-CAD need a display?
The window is the one part of DX-CAD™ that needs a display. Every other command runs on a machine with none.
More: The window
Can I have several documents open at once?
Several documents can be open at once, one tab each. Each tab has its own parts, model pane, undo history and file name, and the Parts and History docks, the title bar and the actions follow the tab in front.
More: Tabs
Where does the model live in the window?
The pane on the right is the model.py, and it is the document's source of truth: the shapes in the scene are what the last run of that text built. Typing in it changes nothing until the model is run.
More: The model pane
Is it safe to open a project someone sent me?
A part or assembly file is something people are sent, and the model inside one is a program. So a project opened from a file is asked about before its model is run for the first time, by Run, by F5 or by Run on Change: the question says that a model is Python and runs with your own permissions, and names the project.
More: The model a project carries
Can I ask the Assistant to build or change a part?
The Assistant dock, along the bottom of the view: type a request and the steps taken to build or change the document show in the chat, each one written into the model and one Undo.
More: The Assistant
How do I get help while I work?
Help > User Guide opens this guide in a window of DX-CAD's own, at its first page.
More: The help window
Where do I find the keyboard shortcuts?
Help > Keyboard Shortcuts: every action that has a shortcut, by menu, action and keys, read from the window's own actions.
More: The Keyboard Shortcuts box
What DX-CAD does not do
What does DX-CAD build its solids with?
DX-CAD™ builds every solid with OpenCASCADE (OCCT), the geometry kernel underneath it; its release notes are at github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/releases.
More: Known limitations
Why is a large fillet refused?
A fillet as big as half the face it runs along leaves nothing of that face between its blends, and OCCT cannot build the solid that would need. DX-CAD refuses it and names the radius.
Workaround: Make the fillet smaller than half the shortest edge it meets, or remove the face first and model the round as a revolve or a sketch arc.
More: Fillets that would consume a face
Why does a fillet fail where several filleted edges meet at a corner?
Where three or more filleted edges meet at a corner, OCCT has to build a corner patch between the blends. When the blends meet in a point, or nearly so, there is no patch to build, and the fillet fails.
Workaround: Give a radius under half the shortest edge that meets the corner, or fillet fewer edges in one call; or chamfer the corner instead.
More: Fillets meeting at a vertex
Can a fillet change its radius along an edge?
DX-CAD's fillets take one radius per call, from the model language, the window and the agent door alike; a blend whose radius changes along its edge is not offered.
Workaround: Split the edge where the radius should change and fillet each part at its own radius, or model the shape as a loft between sketched sections.
More: Variable-radius fillets
Why does a boolean fail when two parts only touch?
When two parts share a face, or touch along a line or at a point, floating-point noise can leave a hairline gap or overlap that OCCT reads as two solids. DX-CAD retries a failed boolean once with a fuzzy tolerance of 0.00001 mm (BOOLEAN_FUZZY_VALUE), which closes such gaps; when that fails too, or the parts only touch along a line or at a point, the boolean is refused rather than leaving two solids or an invalid one.
Workaround: Make the parts overlap by some volume, at least a few hundredths of a millimetre, rather than only touching.
More: Booleans on coincident or tangent faces
Why can a part not always be hollowed out?
Hollowing a part offsets every face inwards by the wall's thickness. Where a feature is thinner than two walls, or a face is a free-form surface whose offset folds over itself, the offset faces cross and OCCT cannot close the shell.
Workaround: Give a wall thinner than half the thinnest feature, or hollow the plain body first and add the thin features after.
More: Shelling and offsets on complex faces
Do face numbers stay the same when an earlier feature changes?
OCCT numbers a solid's faces and edges afresh each time it is built, so "face 7" can be a different face after an earlier feature changes. This is the persistent naming problem every CAD kernel has.
Workaround: DX-CAD does not keep kernel numbers between runs. A model is a script, so each feature is built from the values in it, not from picked faces; mates and references name faces by what they are and where they lie ("hole 1", ">Z", a face picked by position), found again on every run; and each part keeps a stable id of its own in the file, whatever it is renamed.
More: Persistent naming
Does DX-CAD repair STEP files, and does it read IGES?
A STEP file from another program can carry faces whose edges do not quite meet, or solids that are not closed. DX-CAD reads STEP as it is and does not heal it, so such a solid is reported as not valid by OCCT's check, and booleans on it may fail. IGES files are not read at all.
Workaround: Heal or sew the model in the program that wrote it and export it again as closed solids, in STEP (AP214 or AP242).
More: STEP and IGES files that need healing
Can DX-CAD solve all the mates of an assembly at once?
DX-CAD resolves an assembly's mates one at a time, in the order the model writes them, each placing its part against parts already placed. A mate that would need several parts moved at once, such as one closing a loop, or one that disagrees with the mates before it, is refused rather than solved.
Workaround: Write the mates in the order the parts are placed, each part mated to parts before it, and change the order by editing the script.
More: No simultaneous assembly solver
Can DX-CAD work with an assembly of thousands of parts?
Every part is its own full shape in the view and in the file, with no lightweight stand-ins, so an assembly of thousands of parts is slow to open, to turn and to save.
Workaround: Keep sub-assemblies in files of their own and bring them in with use(), working on one at a time.
More: Large assemblies
Can DX-CAD draw a picture of a part on a Mac with no window open?
A picture drawn with no window open (dxcad render, the agent's render_view, the gallery, and the preview a saved part carries for Explorer) needs a hidden native window for OCCT to draw into. On macOS that is a Cocoa window, made on the application's main thread, which DX-CAD does not make without its own window. Such a request is refused there, saying so, and a part saved on macOS has no preview picture.
Workaround: Open the part in DX-CAD's window to see it, or draw its picture on Windows or on Linux. With the window open, the Assistant's render_view and the window link's draw from the window's own view on every platform, so the Assistant looks at the model on a Mac as it does elsewhere; only a picture asked for with no window open is refused there.
More: Pictures without a window on macOS
What happens with the hardest cases, such as a fillet that is too big?
The hard cases DX-CAD is tested against each time, each run as a model.py: booleans of coplanar and tangent faces, blends bigger than their edges allow, shells against what they meet, overlapping patterns, sheet bends of radius 0, tiny text and mates that cannot be met. Each ends in a valid solid or is refused with its reason and what would work instead, never a crash.
More: The robustness suite

DX-CAD by Designmatix Ltd. Last updated 23 October 2026.
In short: DX-CAD collects nothing about you or your work. It makes a request only when you check for updates, use the Assistant, or activate a licence, and each sends only what is listed below. When you buy, Paddle handles the payment; we keep only what we need to issue and check your licence.

Who we are
Designmatix Ltd is the controller of the personal data described here: a company registered in England and Wales under number 12697280, at 71-75 Shelton Street, London WC2H 9JQ, United Kingdom, registered with the Information Commissioner's Office under registration number ZB483460. For anything about your data, email support@designmatix.co.uk.
The DX-CAD program
No telemetry. No usage statistics and no crash reports. Nothing is collected about you, your computer or your work.
Your files stay where you put them. DX-CAD reads and writes only the files you open, save and export.
Update check. Help > Check for Updates asks DX-CAD's public site on GitHub Pages for a small file naming the latest release and compares it with your version on your computer. Nothing is sent but the request itself. Checking at every start is off until you switch it on. GitHub sees the request come from your internet address, under its own privacy policy.
The log stays on your computer (Help > Open Log Folder). It holds the version, the platform, the commands you used and any errors. It is yours to read, delete or attach to a bug report; nothing sends it.
The agent door (dxcad serve) works only on your computer. It listens on a network port only if started with --http, and then only on this computer, for a client holding its token.
The Assistant
The Assistant sends nothing until you switch it on; it asks once, saying what follows. Then each request you type goes to the AI provider you chose, under your own key for that provider: Anthropic (which runs Claude), OpenAI, Azure OpenAI in your company's own tenant, Google Gemini, or an OpenAI-compatible address you give, which for a local model such as Ollama or LM Studio is your own computer. With each request it sends the facts of the document in front of you (its parts, sizes and faces), its model script, the results of the tools the assistant uses, and pictures of the view when the assistant asks for one. Nothing of any other document is sent.
That data goes from your computer to your provider, not to us, under your agreement with that provider and its privacy policy. Your keys stay on your computer, encrypted for your Windows account by Windows' data protection, never in a settings file or the log. A company can limit the providers or switch AI off entirely, and DX-CAD then makes no connection to any AI service.
A hosted option, using a DX-CAD account instead of your own key, is planned. When it is available, this notice will say what it sends to us and to whom we pass it.
Buying and activating a licence
Buying. Our order process is conducted by our online reseller Paddle.com, the Merchant of Record for all our orders. Paddle collects your payment details, billing address and tax information and is responsible for them under its own privacy notice. Paddle tells our licence service your email address, Paddle's customer, subscription and transaction numbers, the products and number of seats you bought, and the dates of your paid period. We never see your card details.
Your licence key is emailed to you by our licence service. If you sign in with an emailed code instead of a key, we use your email address to send the code and find your licences.
Activating. When you activate (Help > Licence), DX-CAD sends our licence service at licence.designmatix.co.uk the key you typed (or your sign-in), a random install number it made for this installation (never a fingerprint of your computer), an optional computer name you choose so you can tell your seats apart, and its version. While a licence is active, DX-CAD sends the signed token the service gave it about once a week to renew it, and when you give a seat back. Nothing else is sent: no name, file or setting. The token is checked on your computer and works offline for up to 14 days.
Launch offer check (version 0.1.0 only). DX-CAD 0.1.0, from 30 days before its launch offer ends, asks for the same public file as the update check at start, to know whether the offer has been extended. Nothing is sent but the request. Version 0.1.1 and later make no such request.

text:
DX-CAD › Python CAD
Models you can read
Python CAD: every 3D model is also a short script
Model in the window with the mouse, or write the part as Python. Either way the model is a readable script you can change, re-run, diff and keep under version control.
Download the 30-day free trial See pricing
A cut-away two-spool turbofan engine, modelled in DX-CAD in Python
Why script your CAD
Change a number, rebuild
Sizes live at the top of the script. Change one and the part rebuilds, holes, patterns, flanges and all.
Variants without copies
One script makes a whole family of parts. Keep it in Git, review changes as diffs, and know exactly what changed between revisions.
Automate the repetitive
Generate the same bracket in twenty sizes, or a product range from a spreadsheet, from the command line, with no window open.
Runs without a window
dxcad run builds a model from the command line, so scripts fit into build servers, batch jobs and your own tools.
What you get
A real CAD kernel
DX-CAD is built on the OpenCASCADE kernel: sketches, extrudes, revolves, booleans, fillets, patterns, assemblies with mates, sheet metal and drawings.
pip install dxcad
DX-CAD installs from PyPI for Python 3.12, as well as from the Windows installer and the macOS and Linux builds.
An open-source SDK
Write add-ons with the Apache-licensed SDK: new commands, kinds of part and drawing tools. See how to build and publish a plugin.
Exchange with any CAD
STEP import and export with assembly structure, names and colours; DXF, STL and 3MF out.
A whole part in 25 lines
A mounting bracket with a row of holes, from DX-CAD's own examples. Every name is already in scope; change a number and run it again.
LENGTH = 80.0
DEPTH = 30.0
HEIGHT = 46.0
THICKNESS = 6.0
HOLES = 4
HOLE_DIAMETER = 5.0
INSET = 10.0
section = (
Sketch(Plane.YZ)
.move_to((0, 0))
.line_to((DEPTH, 0))
.line_to((DEPTH, HEIGHT))
.line_to((DEPTH - THICKNESS, HEIGHT))
.line_to((DEPTH - THICKNESS, THICKNESS))
.line_to((0, THICKNESS))
.close()
)
body = section.extrude(LENGTH)
pitch = (LENGTH - 2 * INSET) / (HOLES - 1)
drill = make_cylinder(HOLE_DIAMETER / 2, THICKNESS, origin=(INSET, (DEPTH - THICKNESS) / 2, 0))
drills = linear_pattern(drill, (pitch, 0, 0), HOLES)
part("bracket", cut_all(body, drills), color="steel")
Questions
Do I have to write Python to use DX-CAD?
No. Everything can be done in the window with the mouse. The script is there when you want it.
Which Python?
Python 3.12. The Windows installer, the macOS app and the Linux AppImage carry their own, so you need no Python of your own unless you install from PyPI.
How do I run a script without the window?
From the command line: dxcad run model.py --output part.dxcprt builds it, and dxcad flat unfolds a sheet part from it.
Is DX-CAD open source?
DX-CAD itself is free for 30 days and then licensed; its SDK, for add-ons, is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

text:
What is new in each release
DX-CAD by Designmatix Ltd. Newest first. The latest is 0.1.6, 13 November 2026.
What each release of DX-CAD brings, in plain words. Each one installs over the one before, and your files, settings and add-ons are kept.
Releases
DX-CAD 0.1.6, 13 November 2026
DX-CAD 0.1.5, 3 November 2026
DX-CAD 0.1.4, 1 November 2026
DX-CAD 0.1.3, 31 October 2026
DX-CAD 0.1.2, 25 October 2026
DX-CAD 0.1.1, 23 October 2026
DX-CAD 0.1.0, 16 October 2026
DX-CAD 0.1.6
13 November 2026
An update to 0.1.5, 13 November 2026. It installs over 0.1.5, and your files, settings and add-ons are kept. Drawings get clearer dimensions you can style, make your own and edit, and title-block values you change where they stand. Long work shows how far it has got and can be cancelled. STEP and DXF files come in through a wizard, mates are edited from the Feature tree, and a model can hold levels, types, hosted elements and schedules. Claude Desktop can be allowed to build models, and changes many lines at once. Add-ons get plugin API 7.
Modelling
Connect Claude Desktop now asks once whether Claude may run models. In 0.1.5 it could change a model's lines but never build it; Allow lets it run a trusted project's model, and Settings > Runs changes your answer.
Claude Desktop changes several places in a model in one step, one undo for the lot, so a change to a big model takes far less time.
File > Import... brings in a STEP file or a DXF drawing step by step, checking what it holds, and its units, before anything is added.
Right-click or double-click a mate in the Feature tree to change its kind and value, or delete it, one undo step.
A model can name levels and grid lines and stand parts on a level, give elements a type whose values they override one by one, host an element in another so it cuts it and moves with it, and list element values in a read-only schedule you can save as CSV. View > Project Browser lists the levels, drawings and schedules.
Drawings
Dimensions keep clear of the views and of their own text. Drawing properties > Dimensions sets the arrow size, text height, gaps and spacing; Settings > Drawings sets them for new drawings.
Make Dimensions Editable turns a view's automatic sizes and hole callouts into dimensions of your own, to move, edit, type over and delete.
Double-click a title-block value on the sheet to change it there.
"Please wait" shows a bar, the percent done and the time left, and Cancel stops an export with nothing written.
The sheet on screen draws what the PDF draws, its texts centred where they belong; a long status message can be read in full by clicking it.
Hidden lines on big assemblies are worked out faster, every line as before.
Measure
Check Interference... can also list the pairs of parts closer than a gap you type, each with its gap and a red line between the nearest points.
Add-ons
Plugin API 7: an add-on's commands can show their progress and be cancelled, be greyed with their own reason and carry tooltips; its drawing views follow the drawing's units and turn by 90 degrees; its sheet tools can take clicks until Enter; and its flat patterns can carry marking on layers of their own and go several to one DXF. Add-ons for buildings can read a model's levels, types, hosts and schedules.
Known limitations
Hidden lines on a very big assembly still take minutes for each view; the quick outline shows meanwhile, with a notice on the sheet.
Those of 0.1.0, below, still hold.
DX-CAD 0.1.5
3 November 2026
An update to 0.1.4, 3 November 2026. It installs over 0.1.4, and your files, settings and add-ons are kept. It makes DX-CAD easier to drive, by you and by an AI assistant such as Claude Desktop: the script editor finds and goes to lines, agents can read and change a model by its lines and frame the view, a project's model runs only once you have trusted it, and saved projects keep their colours and sheet metal. Drawings gain editable, movable title-block texts and dimensions in two units.
Modelling
The script editor: Edit > Go to Line (Ctrl+G), a Find bar (Ctrl+F, F3, Shift+F3) and Replace (Ctrl+H), Replace All being one undo step.
Claude Desktop and other agents can read the script pane, find a line, change only the lines that need changing and run the model, so a small change to a long model no longer means writing the whole model again. They can also set and fit the live view, select and isolate parts, and take a picture of the view as you see it.
File > Trust This Project's Model: a model that came in a project file runs only once you have trusted it, and DX-CAD remembers your answer until the model changes. An agent cannot run it before you do.
Running a model never writes the project file; only Save does. A reopened assembly keeps each part's colour and part number.
Orthographic and perspective views, Fit Selection (Shift+F), arrow keys to pan, zoom about the cursor, and a choice of what the camera does after a run. Zoom Window now fits the box you draw.
Settings > Assistant takes your AI provider's key, tests it and lists the provider's current models. Settings > Runs sets a run's time limit.
Sheet metal
A cut-out of any shape, such as a window with rounded corners, keeps the part as sheet metal, with true arcs in its flat pattern and DXF.
A reopened project's sheet metal parts keep their flat patterns without running the model.
Drawings
Every text in the title block can be edited and moved.
Dimensions in mm, inch, or both (mm [inch] or inch [mm]).
New drawings have no centre marks until you turn them on.
Install
Starting DX-CAD again brings the open window to the front.
Restart Claude Desktop, on the start page, works with the Microsoft Store edition of Claude Desktop.
Known limitations
Those of 0.1.0, below, still hold.
DX-CAD 0.1.4
1 November 2026
An update to 0.1.3, 1 November 2026. It installs over 0.1.3, and your files, settings and add-ons are kept. It mends one thing: Connect Claude Desktop, on the start page, now links Claude Desktop to an installed DX-CAD.
Install
Connect Claude Desktop writes the command Claude Desktop needs to start DX-CAD's server in an installed DX-CAD, on Windows and on a Mac. Before, Claude Desktop could not connect. If you clicked it in an earlier version, click it again in 0.1.4, then restart Claude Desktop.
Known limitations
Those of 0.1.0, below, still hold.
DX-CAD 0.1.3
31 October 2026
An update to 0.1.2, 31 October 2026. It installs over 0.1.2, and your files, settings and add-ons are kept; add-ons made for 0.1.2 work with it. What is new: you can turn a drawing view by 90 degrees, cut holes and slots across a bend in sheet metal, and add-ons can have toolbars of their own; the macOS app opens without the "could not verify" box, and a few things you may have met are fixed.
Sheet metal
Holes, rounded slots and cutouts across a bend: give them on the flat pattern with bend_cut, and they are cut as the shop floor cuts them, straight through each wall and wrapped round the bend. A cut may cross several bends in a row. Cut in the window, through one face and on across a bend, now keeps the part as sheet metal instead of being refused.
The flat pattern breaks a bend line only where a cut across the bend crosses it; other holes and openings leave it whole, as in 0.1.2.
Drawings
Turn a drawing view by 90, 180 or 270 degrees: set Rotation in Drawing properties' View group, or right-click the view and choose Rotate 90 Anticlockwise or Rotate 90 Clockwise. Undo turns it back. The view turns about its centre, its sizes and notes turn with it and stay readable, and the DXF and PDF show it turned. The drawing keeps the turn when saved.
The first command that needs a drawing's view regions, such as Drafting Pro's Balloon View, no longer waits several seconds: they are worked out while the drawing opens, and the window answers clicks all the while.
Add-ons
An add-on can put its commands on toolbars of its own, listed in View > Toolbars, and a toolbar can show only on the tabs it is for, a drafting add-on's only while a drawing is in front. Hidden that way, it stays ticked in View > Toolbars, which keeps your own choice.
An add-on you downloaded twice, which the browser saved as ... (1).whl, installs from Help > Add-ons > Install from File. What a wheel is built for is read from inside it, not from its file's name.
Help > Add-ons shows the whole Licence text, "Free during your 30-day trial (ends ...)", with its date, on Windows, macOS and Linux.
The SDK's plugin API is 5: an add-on's marks on a turned view turn with it.
Install
The macOS app is signed and notarised, so it opens without the "could not verify" box. For a build that is not, the install page gives macOS 15's way: System Settings > Privacy & Security, then Open Anyway.
dxcad serve --window started before DX-CAD is open waits for the window instead of giving up, and says in its log why it stopped.
Known limitations
Those of 0.1.0, below, still hold.
DX-CAD 0.1.2
25 October 2026
An update to 0.1.1, 25 October 2026. It installs over 0.1.1, and your files, settings and add-ons are kept; add-ons made for 0.1.1 work with it.
Sheet metal
Rounded slots, at any angle, through a sheet part's base or a flange's leg: draw one with the slot tool inside Base Flange's outline, type it on the Flange dialog's Slots line, or Cut one through a face, which keeps the part as sheet metal. The flat pattern and its DXF show each slot as two lines and two arcs, and the cut length counts them.
Add-ons
Installing or removing an add-on says so in a message box. Until you restart DX-CAD, the add-ons list shows a new version as "(after restart)", since the one running is still the old one.
The add-ons are "Free during your 30-day trial", with the day it ends.
Fabrication's shape dialogs and Drafting Pro's sheet tools work in the installed DX-CAD: it now carries every module an add-on may use. A sheet tool that cannot follow the mouse says so on the status bar.
Licensing
Licences (a paid subscription) are available from 1 November 2026. Until then, Help > Licence's Activate, Send code and Sign in say so and contact nothing; DX-CAD and its add-ons cost nothing until your trial ends. No trial ends before 16 November 2026.
When the licence service cannot be reached, Help > Licence says so in one plain sentence.
The Licence box shows every line in full and says each date once. Deactivate is greyed unless a licence is activated on this computer.
Known limitations
Those of 0.1.0, below, still hold.
DX-CAD 0.1.1
23 October 2026
An update to 0.1.0, 23 October 2026. It installs over 0.1.0, and your files, settings and add-ons are kept.
Modelling
The Assistant reads the whole of your model.py, where the provider you chose has room for it, not only its first 6,000 characters.
A long request to the Assistant, or a long reply, no longer makes the window wider than the screen. The Undo button says the start of a long answer's name; the Edit menu and the button's tooltip say all of it.
Add-ons
During your trial, the add-ons show in the menus and say where to download them; an add-on you have installed shows its menu once, with no greyed copy beside it.
The SDK gives an add-on the licence words DX-CAD shows, with the trial's dates.
Licensing
Free for 30 days from first start, then a licence. Opening, viewing and exporting stay free. This plain 30-day trial replaces 0.1.0's offer; if you first started DX-CAD under 0.1.0, you keep the date 0.1.0's licence gave you, or your 30 days if they end later.
The paid add-ons, Fabrication and Drafting Pro, are free during your trial too, while you hold no licence key.
Activate and Deactivate never freeze the window, and a network failure is said in one plain line. A paid licence that has run out says so, rather than that the trial has ended.
The licence is checked online every 8 hours while DX-CAD is open.
Setting the computer's clock back does not unlock editing, a clock set ahead by mistake never locks it, and deleting DX-CAD's settings does not start the trial again.
Install
DX-CAD looks for a newer version as it starts and says so on the status bar; File > Settings switches that off.
Windows Explorer shows thumbnails and icons for .dxcprt, .dxcasm and .dxcdrg files, and the installer replaces its thumbnail handler even while Explorer is using it.
Double-clicking dxcad.exe says what it is and opens DX-CAD, and leaves no empty terminal window behind.
Help > About shows every line at 200 percent display scaling.
The macOS app is signed and notarised in the order Apple asks for, and the Linux wheel is one PyPI accepts.
Known limitations
Those of 0.1.0, below, still hold.
DX-CAD 0.1.0
16 October 2026
The first public release, 16 October 2026. Under its licence (EULA.md) as 0.1.0 shipped it, DX-CAD was free for any use, at work too, until the date that licence gave, or until your 30-day trial ended if that was later; 0.1.1 replaces this with a plain 30-day trial from first start (see 0.1.1, above). After that, editing and saving need a licence; opening, viewing and exporting your files stay free. Help > Licence says where you stand. The SDK that add-ons are built on is open source under Apache 2.0.
Modelling
Every part is a model.py you can read, change and run again. Boxes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori; sketches extruded and revolved; fuse, cut and common; fillets, chamfers, holes, countersinks and counterbores; shells, lofts, sweeps, drafts, mirrors and patterns; and 3D text, raised or cut. What you do in the window is written into the model as you do it.
A sketcher with lines, rectangles, circles, arcs, polygons, slots, ellipses and splines, corner fillets and chamfers, offset, mirror, trim and break, sizes typed while you draw, and constraints.
Parts, assemblies and drawings are three kinds of file (.dxcprt, .dxcasm, .dxcdrg), each in a tab of its own; tabs can be tiled side by side. Recent files, part colours, part numbers, revisions and your own properties.
Assemblies: parts placed by numbers or by mates (coincident, concentric, distance, angle), parts used from their own files, sub-assemblies, a bill of materials and an interference check. Mates are suggested from matching features, and you confirm each one.
Move a part by dragging it, hide and show parts, section the view with a cutting plane, and spin it on a turntable.
Out to the shop: parts to STEP, STL, 3MF and BREP, flat patterns to DXF and SVG, a printability report, and Send to Slicer.
An Assistant panel that builds and changes parts from what you type, with your own API key; each answer is one step of Undo.
Autosave: after a crash, DX-CAD offers back what you had open.
Sheet metal
Base flanges from a closed sketch, arcs and circles included; flanges on any edge, on a flange's own edges too, with corners that never overlap; hems (open, closed and teardrop) and returns in or out at any angle.
One dialog per command, with a diagram and a live preview. The Flange dialog takes all edges at once, or a length per edge in its table, and edits a flange you made before.
Thickness, bend radius and K-factor from material and gauge tables.
The flat pattern: Show Flat Pattern switches the view between formed and flat, with bend lines, the blank size, bend-line distances and a bend table; Export Flat Pattern writes DXF or SVG for a laser or a plasma table, with shop profiles, and dxcad flat writes the flat as a STEP solid too.
Drawings
A drawing is a document of its own, drawn again from its model whenever the model changes. Ten ISO and ANSI title blocks, on ISO sheets from A4 to A0 and ANSI sheets A to D, fonts and text heights, linetypes.
Front, top, right and isometric views, with hidden lines when you want them; Add View for any other, a view at a scale of its own, and Add Part Sheets for a sheet per part. Views move as you drag them and stay in line with the front unless you unlock them.
Overall sizes, hole callouts and a parts list with item, part number, description, material, quantity and revision, and mass or size when you add those columns.
Lines and polylines drawn by hand on the sheet.
Out to PDF and DXF.
Large assemblies (a hundred parts and more) open quickly on a drawing.
Measure
View > Measure: distance, angle, radius, diameter, length and area by picking points, edges and faces, in the 3D view, in a sketch and on a drawing. The status bar says what to pick next; the result shows beside the picks, on the status bar and in the Measure panel, with Copy.
Add-ons
Help > Add-ons... installs, lists, turns on and off and removes add-ons, from inside DX-CAD; installing a newer version over the old one updates it.
DX-CAD Fabrication (cones, transitions, elbows, branches, weldments and more) and DX-CAD Drafting Pro (dimensions, balloons, tolerances, GD&T, section and detail views, revision tables and notes) are paid add-ons; every paid command shows in the menus, greyed, with its add-on's name. Both are unlocked, with no key, through your 30-day trial while you hold no licence; then each needs a licence of its own. Until an add-on is installed, its greyed commands and Help > Add-ons say where to download it while it is free, and where to buy it after that.
An add-on brings its own menus, toolbar buttons, dialogs, drawing views and tools, and its own help: F1 in its command shows its steps. A command that does not apply to the tab in front is greyed, and its tooltip says why.
Agents: dxcad serve is an MCP server, and Claude Desktop can drive the open window through it; Connect Claude Desktop sets it up in one click. Every operation is on the command line too.
Install
Windows: an installer, or a portable zip that needs no Python; both carry dxcad.exe, the command line.
macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux (x64) builds.
pip install dxcad on Python 3.12.
dxcad doctor tells you the install works, ending with SMOKE OK, and dxcad doctor --report gives everything a bug report needs.
A start page of example parts, six tutorials, and help on every command (F1, or the ? button in a dialog). How each build is installed and opened is in docs/install.md.
Known limitations
Add-on authors: document.view_lines(view, parts="all") names every part a drawn line lies on, but where one part is sunk inside another with no edge of its own on the line (the gearbox example's sight-glass lens in its bezel, a nameplate's letters in the plate) the hidden part is not named. document.view_regions(view) gives the part seen in each region of a view correctly, those included.
STEP files keep assembly structure, names, colours, part numbers and properties, both ways; whether another CAD program shows those properties has not yet been checked.
Pictures of DX-CAD files in Windows Explorer's large icons and preview pane have not yet been checked on a real desktop.
The macOS and Linux builds come from CI and have not yet been run by hand. The macOS build is not yet signed by Apple; it opens as docs/install.md says.
The Assistant's picture of the open window on macOS has not yet been checked by hand. On macOS a picture drawn with no window open (dxcad render, the agent's render_view) is refused, and a part saved there carries no preview picture.
Mates are placed in order, one after another: there is no solver that moves parts together, and no joints or motion.
What the kernel cannot do, and how DX-CAD says so, is in docs/limitations.md.

title: DX-CAD SDK: plugins, documentation and file format | DX-CAD by Designmatix
text:
DX-CAD SDK
Designmatix Ltd. Last updated 30 October 2026.
Get the SDK. The source is on GitHub at github.com/faizaldm/DX-CAD-SDK, the package is pip install dxcad-sdk, and the documentation, with the DX-CAD file format specification, is at faizaldm.github.io/DX-CAD-SDK.
What the SDK is
The DX-CAD SDK lets you write plugins for DX-CAD in Python: new commands, menus and toolbars in the window, new kinds of part, tools for the Assistant and new drawing annotations. It contains the public plugin interface, a checker that tells you whether a plugin uses only that interface (dxcad-sdk check), a project template to start from, and its documentation.
DX-CAD's own add-ons, Fabrication and Drafting Pro, are built on the same interface.
Build and publish a DX-CAD plugin: a step-by-step guide, from the template to a wheel your users install from Help > Add-ons.
Licence
The SDK is a separate work from DX-CAD, under the Apache License 2.0, given in its own LICENSE file. The DX-CAD licence agreement does not cover it.
The DX-CAD file format
The specification of DX-CAD's files (parts, assemblies and drawings) is published here with the SDK, so that other programs can read and write them. Section 3 of the licence agreement explains how it relates to your rights under the law.
Where to find it
SDK source code and releases: github.com/faizaldm/DX-CAD-SDK, and the package dxcad-sdk on PyPI.
Documentation: faizaldm.github.io/DX-CAD-SDK, with the plugins page.
How to build and publish a plugin: the guide.
